entries.name: Armored Hulk
entries.description: Some barbarians disdain the hides and leather used as armor by most of their kin. Instead they master the heaviest of armors, even those created by more civilized people, to gain greater protection and stability in battle.

entries.name: Beastkin Berserker
entries.description: While some barbarians take on bestial aspects in their rages, the beastkin berserker descends so deeply into primal fury that she actually transforms into an animal.

entries.name: Breaker
entries.description: Breakers find the need to destroy their surroundings.

entries.name: Brutal Pugilist
entries.description: Some barbarians focus on using their bare hands to tear their opponents limb from limb.

entries.name: Brutish Swamper
entries.description: The hardy and insular denizens of the swamp produce warriors of narrow focus and great strength.

entries.name: Cave Dweller
entries.description: Unused to the light of the sun, cave dwellers use their subterranean expertise to protect their clans from the manifold dangers of deep caverns and tunnels.

entries.name: Deepwater Rager
entries.description: Deepwater ragers bellow ferociously as they charge their enemies, tackling them into the raging seas.

entries.name: Dreadnought
entries.description: Unstoppable and fearless, the dreadnought turns the terror of her enemies into violent physical power.

entries.name: Drunken Brute
entries.description: Drunken brutes use potent liquor to fuel their rage and grant them additional powers.

entries.name: Drunken Rager
entries.description: These hotheaded, hard-drinking ruffians and brawlers are as dangerous in the midst of combat as they are in a tavern, and they wouldn’t be caught dead without a libation for either occasion.

entries.name: Elemental Kin
entries.description: Some barbarian tribes have strong ties to the elemental forces of nature.

entries.name: Fearsome Defender
entries.description: These savage slaves feel little pain and exist only to rain terror down on the enemies of their pitiless masters.

entries.name: Feral Gnasher
entries.description: Feral gnashers grow up in the wild, either raised by animals or scraping by on their own, and soon learn to fend for themselves.

entries.name: Flesheater
entries.description: A flesheater eats flesh to create a spiritual bond between herself and the consumed creature, allowing her to take on aspects of the creature that served as the meal.

entries.name: Geminate Invoker
entries.description: Geminate invokers are barbarians who use Rivethun traditions to invite spirits into their bodies.

entries.name: Giant Stalker
entries.description: Giant stalkers are followers of the a savage tribe who have trained since childhood to spot and track giants.

entries.name: Hateful Rager
entries.description: From a young age, many half-orcs are treated cruelly, bullied, ridiculed, and made outcasts. While some hide their shame, others foster a deep, burning hatred that they channel into a raw fury and unleash against their enemies.

entries.name: Hurler
entries.description: The hurler becomes skilled at throwing objects at their foes before closing in for the kill.

entries.name: Invulnerable Rager
entries.description: Some barbarians learn to take whatever comes their way, shrugging off mortal wounds with ease.

entries.name: Jungle Rager
entries.description: A jungle rager can disappear from sight, strike from hiding, and use the environment to shield herself from harm.

entries.name: Mad Dog
entries.description: Though named for the wild savages who fight alongside rabid dogs, mad dogs employ all manner of beasts as their battle brethren.

entries.name: Mooncursed
entries.description: Some barbarians exhibit an unusual form of lycanthropy powered by their fury. Such a character transforms willfully but can maintain her animal or hybrid forms only while raging.

entries.name: Mounted Fury
entries.description: Many barbarian tribes are masters of the horse, teaching their members how to ride from a young age.

entries.name: Numerian Liberator
entries.description: While many native Kellids oppose the Technic League and its espousal of foul alien artifacts, the most stalwart and staunchly dedicated of these technophobic traditionalists refer to themselves as Numerian liberators.

entries.name: Pack Hunter
entries.description: Pack hunter barbarians team up to hunt dangerous prey to feed, to protect their camps, and as a rite of passage.

entries.name: Pack Rager
entries.description: Barbarian rages can be a thing of savage beauty, exhibiting a lethal grace. While such uncontrolled displays of carnage often disregard group tactics, there are those barbarians whose rages inspire and spur on their allies during the ferocious dance of death.

entries.name: Primal Hunter
entries.description: Rather than exploding with anger, primal hunters focus their rage to strike distant targets.

entries.name: Raging Cannibal
entries.description: While savagery is not inherently evil, some barbaric cultures thrive on depravity and welcome the act of feeding on their own kind.

entries.name: Savage Barbarian
entries.description: The savage barbarian learns to avoid blows and toughen up their skin.

entries.name: Savage Technologist
entries.description: Savage technologists exhort Kellids to rise up against the depredations of the Technic League. But rather than rejecting technology, they wield the League’s own weapons against it.

entries.name: Scarred Rager
entries.description: The scarred rager believes each wound tells the tales of her prowess and bravery.

entries.name: Sea Reaver
entries.description: Some sea reavers are no more than hunters of the open sea, while others are raiders striking fear into coastal settlements within reach of the sea reavers’ longships.

entries.name: Sharptooth
entries.description: Coastal hunters and agents of the ocean’s rage, sharptooth barbarians emulate the greatest predators of the sea.

entries.name: Superstitious
entries.description: The superstitious barbarian is naturally distrusting, developing keen senses to protect themselves from harm.

entries.name: Titan Mauler
entries.description: In lands overrun by giants, dragons, and other hulking beasts, entire fellowships of barbarians hone tactics and traditions with one purpose—to bring low these massive foes.

entries.name: Totem Warrior
entries.description: The totem warrior has a special totem that is the patron of her tribe.

entries.name: True Primitive
entries.description: Isolated and xenophobic tribes that dwell in areas untouched by civilization often see anything from cities and organized settlements as strange, dangerous, and decadent.

entries.name: Untamed Rager
entries.description: There are no rules in the wild. Some barbarians enter combat with only victory in mind and do anything in their power to achieve it.

entries.name: Urban Barbarian
entries.description: Every barbarian knows that city life can soften the spirit and the body, but some barbarians take on the trappings and ways of their adoptive homes and bend their savage powers to its challenges.

entries.name: Wild Rager
entries.description: Rages are barely controlled, but there are those who wholly give in to their more savage side, letting their rages take them to a confusing and uncontrolled place of terrible savagery.

entries.name: Wildborn
entries.description: Some barbarians are born or bred outside the reach of civilization. These wildborn fight and survive without ever seeing a forge or worked stone, and only dare a trip into the city when no other option is available.

entries.name: Animal Speaker
entries.description: An animal speaker focuses not on the ears and minds of humans, but on the creatures of the wild and those in the underbellies of cities.

entries.name: Arcane Duelist
entries.description: A master of the martial applications of steel and spell, the arcane duelist blends both into a lethal combination.

entries.name: Arcane Healer
entries.description: Though bards may have different reasons for wanting to heal the sick and injured, both out of pure altruism and in order to keep adventuring companions safe, the ability to heal also makes it much easier for a bard to pose as a cleric or other divine healer, opening the door for a wide array of swindles and scams.

entries.name: Archaeologist
entries.description: No stodgy researcher, this archaeologist meets his research head-on in the field.

entries.name: Archivist
entries.description: Some bards greatly prefer academic pursuits to the drama (and sometimes melodrama) of their artistic brethren.

entries.name: Argent Voice
entries.description: Argent voices are agents of the Silver Ravens that dedicate themselves to the study of the magical performance are known as the "Song of Silver".

entries.name: Arrowsong Minstrel
entries.description: Arrowsong minstrels combine the elven traditions of archery, song, and spellcasting into a seamless harmony of dazzling magical effects.

entries.name: Averaka Arbiter
entries.description: Some Averakan bards make it their mission to unify their fellow half-orcs, and are equally skilled at helping allies defeat common enemies and at building a new civilization that reflects their unique identity.

entries.name: Brazen Deceiver
entries.description: Where other thieves use stealth or intimidation to achieve their goals, the brazen deceiver depends on lies backed by powerful shadow magic.

entries.name: Buccaneer
entries.description: A buccaneer is a pirate who specializes in raiding ships and port towns, but who leaves his victims alive whenever possible.

entries.name: Busker
entries.description: A busker uses his dazzling physical stunts to get by on his own in the city streets.

entries.name: Celebrity
entries.description: Known for being known, a celebrity bard is a master of performance who captures the imagination and attention of his audience.

entries.name: Chronicler of Worlds
entries.description: A chronicler of worlds forsakes morality in service of understanding; she is both warrior and mystic, scholar and soldier.

entries.name: Court Bard
entries.description: The court bard takes up the role of resplendent proclaimer and artist-in-residence at the hand of nobility, royalty, and the well-moneyed elite who aspire to join their ranks.

entries.name: Court Fool
entries.description: The court fool holds up an unflattering mirror to those in charge or speaks truths, however veiled, that no one else can safely utter.

entries.name: Cultivator
entries.description: Cultivators use music to promote plant growth and influence the behavior of plants both naturally and supernaturally.

entries.name: Daredevil
entries.description: As quick at wordplay as at swordplay, daredevils are dashing heroes, inspiring their allies to match their clever repartee and acrobatic feats.

entries.name: Dawnflower Dervish
entries.description: Many bards of a sun goddess's faith hone their skills with dance and scimitar to become dervish dancers.

replaces: Bardic Performance, Bardic Knowledge, Lore Master, Dirge of Doom

entries.name: Demagogue
entries.description: Not content with providing amusing and occasionally instructive performances, the demagogue seeks to inflame and ignite his audience.

entries.name: Dervish Dancer
entries.description: Not all bards inspire others with their performances. Dervish dancers enter a near-mystical trance that allows them to push their bodies beyond normal limits.

entries.name: Detective
entries.description: Piecing together clues and catching the guilty with sheer cleverness, the detective is skilled at divining the truth.

entries.name: Dirge Bard
entries.description: A composer of sonorous laments for the dead and elaborate requiems for those lost yet long remembered, dirge bards master musical tools and tropes that must appeal to the ears and hearts of both the living and the dead.

entries.name: Disciple of the Forked Tongue
entries.description: (Vishkanya) Studied in venomous words as well as venomous blood, a disciple of the forked tongue knows just the right phrase to slowly poison the soul.

entries.name: Dragon Herald
entries.description: Dragon heralds are messengers and evangelists of true dragonkind. They carry the word of their dragon patrons far and wide, whether that’s a message of peace or a declaration of war.

entries.name: Dragon Yapper
entries.description: Kobolds’ yammering songs distract opponents in combat, hindering their ability to attack.

entries.name: Duettist
entries.description: Whether singing a delicate duo with a nightingale or slipping coins from purses while a trained monkey distracts the crowd, the duettist blends his bond to his familiar with his natural talent for performance to create amazing effects.

entries.name: Dwarven Scholar
entries.description: A dwarven scholar researches the lineage of the kings of the old dwarven empires and learns their ancient tactics.

entries.name: Faith Singer
entries.description: Faith singers show their faith in their deity with songs or other appropriate performances.

entries.name: Fey Courtier
entries.description: (Gathlain) Fey who associate with courts often become bards skilled at navigating the inhuman societies of the trackless wilds.

entries.name: Fey Prankster
entries.description: Sly and mischievous like the Lantern King himself, fey pranksters learn supernatural tricks that can cause their victims to suffer mishaps and accidents.

entries.name: Filidh
entries.description: By tapping into the world’s natural music, specialized bards known as filidhs are able to see not only the tapestry of life but divine portents of the future from the rhythm of all life’s song.

entries.name: First World Minstrel
entries.description: The First World minstrel's performances channel the mysterious powers of the First World.

entries.name: Flame Dancer
entries.description: A flame dancer studies the movements of fire, adding its grace to his repertoire.

entries.name: Flamesinger
entries.description: The flamesinger finds inspiration in the mesmerizing beauty of fire.

entries.name: Fortune-Teller
entries.description: Instead of using song and dance, a fortune-teller influences people by divining their fate.

entries.name: Geisha
entries.description: Specially trained entertainers called geisha are praised for their appearance and skill at conversation, music, dancing, singing, poetry, and calligraphy.

entries.name: Hatharat Agent
entries.description: Although the Hatharat employs all manner of specialists, bards who take up the role of agent are among its most infamous and widespread.

entries.name: Hoaxer
entries.description: Hoaxers specialize in creating valuable-looking counterfeits and infusing these false treasures with dangerous magic to make their marks more vulnerable to future swindles.

entries.name: Impervious Messenger
entries.description: The impervious messenger is capable of harnessing the unique qualities of bardic magic to keep, transport, and communicate the most precious of secrets and messages.

entries.name: Juggler
entries.description: Jugglers are masters of manipulating objects, most famously by keeping multiple objects in the air simultaneously.

entries.name: Lotus Geisha
entries.description: The lotus geisha of Minkai are renowned for their powers of seduction.

entries.name: Luring Piper
entries.description: Some bards have an exceptional ability to use their musical performances to entrance the world’s wilder creatures.

entries.name: Magician
entries.description: A magician dabbles in performance, but sees it as a means to tap into universal energies and channel them.

entries.name: Masked Performer
entries.description: The masked performer takes on the persona represented by the likeness she wears.

entries.name: Mute Musician
entries.description: A mute musician forswears speech for the unnatural songs and thunderous silences of the depths of space.

entries.name: Negotiator
entries.description: Negotiators are those bards who take the skills of a performer and apply them to the realms of business and law.

entries.name: Phrenologist
entries.description: The phrenologist is an expert at reading creatures’ skulls, and he learns to use this knowledge to his benefit.

entries.name: Pitax: Academy of Grand Arts
entries.description: Those who have successfully mastered the strict curriculum of the Academy of Grand Arts.

entries.name: Plant Speaker
entries.description: Plant speakers build upon their racial plantspeech ability and their storytelling tendencies to create an art form full of deep metaphors and allegory rather than specific details and facts.

entries.name: Prankster
entries.description: The prankster sees humor as the highest form or art, and pranks as the highest form of humor.

entries.name: Provocateur
entries.description: Provocateurs are bards who use their art to make controversial political statements, undermine enemies’ reputations, and upset the status quo on a large scale.

entries.name: Ringleader (AG)
entries.description: Ringleaders are specialists who oversee large operations in which trouble could strike at any moment and any place.

entries.name: Ringleader (UI)
entries.description: Ringleaders are adept in getting the most out of their allies, and they excel at planning for unexpected complications in advance.

entries.name: Sandman
entries.description: Combining performance with stealth, trickery, and guile, the sandman uses cleverness to keep others off-balance.

entries.name: Savage Skald
entries.description: Far from civilization, furious tribes have their own war-singers, work-chanters, and lore-keepers, savaging enemies with song and sword alike.

entries.name: Sea Singer
entries.description: The sea singer calls the blue waters his home, and is much in demand among sea captains wishing good fortune for their crew and hull as they ply the tradewinds far and wide.

entries.name: Shadow Puppeteer
entries.description: A shadow puppeteer invokes amazing and terrifying shadow puppet shows, producing supernatural effects by creating and manipulating shadow.

entries.name: Silver Balladeer
entries.description: The bright purity of silver makes beautiful music, and its vibrations are also anathema to unnatural creatures. Some bards use a mixture of silver-stringed instruments and esoteric knowledge to battle the dark forces of the world.

entries.name: Solacer
entries.description: Solacers are experts in the healing arts as well as creators of performances that console the distraught, rally the stricken, raise spirits, and vanquish sorrow.

entries.name: Songhealer
entries.description: The songhealer brings peace and surcease of pain, calming wild emotions and providing a balm for the wounded body.

entries.name: Sorrowsoul
entries.description: While most bards, on occasion, sing mournful tunes or craft elegies that depict the deepest sadness or the most profound suffering, the sorrowsoul has known tragedy and loss on a level so intimate, he has bound it to his soul.

entries.name: Sound Striker
entries.description: They say that words can cut deeper than any blade, and the sound striker proves this true.

entries.name: Speaker of the Palatine Eye
entries.description: speaker of the Palatine Eye influences others using his occult knowledge rather than the boisterous enthusiasm of most bards.

entries.name: Stonesinger
entries.description: Stonesingers are rare bards capable of vocalizing their bardic performances through subsonic harmonies, allowing their performances to carry as subtle vibrations through stone, rather than through the air.

entries.name: Street Performer
entries.description: Whether acrobat, troubadour, or thespian, the street performer mixes with the masses, singing for his supper.

entries.name: Studious Librarian
entries.description: Studious librarians are bards that have studied long in great libraries of the inner sea region.

entries.name: Thundercaller
entries.description: Thundercallers bear the knowledge of the ancients, wielding it like a weapon to protect the land for which they care so deeply.

entries.name: Voice of Brigh
entries.description: The Whisper in Bronze sometimes sends inspiration to her favorite followers in the form of music

entries.name: Voice of the Wild
entries.description: Most bards are inspired by the art of civilization, yet the voice of the wild’s muse is the grandeur and beauty of nature.

entries.name: Wasteland Chronicler
entries.description: Wasteland chroniclers explore the farthest reaches of desolate wastelands, seeking to unlock the mysteries found there and meet the inhabitants of such regions

entries.name: Watersinger
entries.description: The watersinger’s song reaches from the depths of his soul into the elemental waters from which life first sprang.

replaces: Fascinate, Suggestion, Mass Suggestion, Inspire Competence, 5th-level Lore Master

entries.name: Wit
entries.description: The wit is a master of clever repartee and verbal dueling, moving through noble courts like a fish through water.

entries.name: Angelfire Apostle
entries.description: Angelfire apostles use the powers of good to avoid violence when possible and cleanse both maladies and evil creatures with blinding flames.

entries.name: Appeaser
entries.description: A rare few seek the power of dark forces for brighter ends by focusing on the utilitarian aspects of a god’s portfolio, appeasing their deities through high praise and glorifying their chosen gods’ unaligned aspects.

entries.name: Asmodean Advocate
entries.description: For the faithful of a tyrant god, the words used in a negotiation or contract matter more than their intent.

entries.name: Blossoming Light
entries.description: Blossoming lights are clerics who take their pursuit of purity and light to extremes.

entries.name: Cardinal
entries.description: Cardinals wield significant political power, engaging in the game of intrigue on behalf of their churches

entries.name: Channeler of the Unknown
entries.description: (Ex-cleric archetype) Channelers of the unknown are those faithless clerics who channel the power of an unknown entity or force of the universe

entries.name: Cloistered Cleric
entries.description: Cloistered clerics typically live in a temple and rarely interact with the outside world. They are bookish and well learned in the lore of the faith, paying less attention to its magical and martial aspects.

entries.name: Crashing Wave
entries.description: Clerics who live in or near the sea sometimes embrace the watery aspect of a god of nature over the deity’s other dimensions and take the title of crashing wave; such clerics understand the tempestuousness and cruelty of the sea, but also its generosity and bounty

entries.name: Crusader
entries.description: Crusaders serve the militant arm of a church, ready to stand guard over the religion’s holy places and to be its swift, avenging arm against those who resist its truth.

entries.name: Demonic Apostle
entries.description: Demon worship is common among the drow, and so are ranks of demonic apostles, who gain magical insight from their dark lords and crush their chaotic masters’ enemies by channeling demonic energy.

entries.name: Divine Paragon
entries.description: Divine paragons strive to emulate their god’s ideals as closely as possible.

entries.name: Divine Scourge
entries.description: Divine scourges take on the role of dealing out unique punishments on behalf of their deities, taking pleasure in carrying out their sacrosanct duties.

entries.name: Divine Strategist
entries.description: The divine strategist leads the armies of the faithful, not from the front lines but through her clever strategy and tactical acumen.

entries.name: Ecclesitheurge
entries.description: Eschewing physical armor for protection via the strength of his faith, an ecclesitheurge focuses on the miracles his deity bestows and the breadth of that deity’s dominion.

entries.name: Elder Mythos Cultist
entries.description: Typically grasping, secretive, and thoroughly mad, Elder Mythos cultists open their bodies and minds to horrifying realities not meant for the sane as they strive to prepare the world for the eventual return of their alien masters.

entries.name: Evangelist
entries.description: The evangelist is the voice of her religion in the world.

entries.name: Fiendish Vessel
entries.description: Fiendish vessels, through their fiendish heritage, share an innate connection with their patron, and that connection grants them understanding and power.

entries.name: Forgemaster
entries.description: Forgemasters are priestly dwarves who are ritual casters and expert enchanters, able to produce their rune-graven armaments with astonishing speed.

entries.name: Foundation of Faith
entries.description: Whether aiding the faithful or defending against the depredations of unbelievers, a foundation of faith is unshakable in her convictions.

entries.name: Herald Caller
entries.description: Unlike warpriests or paladins, who charge headlong into battle in the name of their patron deities, herald callers are adept at calling powerful outsiders to aid their brethren in battle.

entries.name: Hidden Priest
entries.description: When practicing their religion is outlawed, the hidden priest learns to hide their true nature and practice magic in secret.

entries.name: Idealist
entries.description: Idealist clerics are personifications of belief, each embracing the purest ideal of his deity’s realm.

entries.name: Iron Priest
entries.description: Iron priests preach of the messengers from beyond the stars, envoys of the divine brought to the world in a falling star.

entries.name: Lawspeaker
entries.description: Lawspeakers spread their philosophy of certain and unwavering justice throughout the inner sea region.

entries.name: Mendevian Priest
entries.description: Crusade-minded clerics of a goddess of valor, a god of war, and other churches come to a crusader nation to learn battlefield tactics and the weaknesses of demons.

entries.name: Merciful Healer
entries.description: The merciful healer is a master of battlefield revivification, sustaining and restoring allies to keep them in the fight.

entries.name: Roaming Exorcist
entries.description: The roaming exorcist travels far and wide to root out possessions, hauntings, and hidden evils. The roaming exorcist extracts unruly spirits from not only victims of possession, but also haunted sites and accursed items.

entries.name: Sacred Attendant
entries.description: Sacred attendants bring out the varied beauty in everyone they help, and they typically worship deities of beauty, love, and sex.

entries.name: Scroll Scholar
entries.description: Those who trade some of their potential to better understand ancient texts and scrolls can become learned scroll scholars.

replaces: 1st Level Domain Power, Channel Energy 5th level increase, 4th-level spell slot

entries.name: Separatist
entries.description: A radical cleric, unsatisfied with the orthodoxy of her deity’s teachings, forges her own path of defiant divine expression.

entries.name: Stoic Caregiver
entries.description: Stoic caregivers are champions of life in defiance of untimely death as well as undeath.

entries.name: Theologian
entries.description: A theologian is an expert on one particular area of her religion

entries.name: Triadic Priest
entries.description: Power comes not just from communion with one’s deity, but also from the formation of divine triumvirates. At the head of these groups are triadic priests.

entries.name: Undead Lord
entries.description: An undead lord is a cleric focused on using necromancy to control undead.

entries.name: Aerie Protector
entries.description: The aerie protector guards nature’s nests and lairs in the highest mountains, and she is only ever truly at ease when under vast expanses of open sky.

entries.name: Ancient Guardian
entries.description: Ancient guardians revere nature and draw power from its divine energies, but also protect the customs, histories, and lore of their tribe and race.

entries.name: Ape Shaman
entries.description: A shaman with this totem calls upon the mighty ape, a peaceful but powerful simian whose strength is beyond compare.

entries.name: Aquatic Druid
entries.description: Shepherds of the lakes and seas, aquatic druids guard ecosystems ranging from shallows streams to deep ocean trenches, ministering to their residents and communing with the tides.

entries.name: Arctic Druid
entries.description: An arctic druid watches over the stark landscape of the far frozen reaches of the world.

entries.name: Ashvawg Tamer
entries.description: Ashvawg Tamers are druids who have chosen to bond with a strange and monstrous creature.

replaces: Resist Nature's Lure, one less Wild Shape/day, Venom Immunity

entries.name: Bat Shaman
entries.description: The bat shaman’s totem is the agile bat, flitting and turning with incredible speed through even the most convoluted mazes.

entries.name: Bear Shaman
entries.description: A shaman with this focus calls upon the mighty bear, titan of the woodlands and mountains, a paragon of strength and ferocity, and yet also a quiet protector rich in wisdom.

entries.name: Blight Druid
entries.description: The devoted servants of nature corrupted, ruined, and destroyed, blight druids are the caretakers of lands ravaged by natural disaster.

entries.name: Boar Shaman
entries.description: A boar shaman chooses the stolid and ferocious boar as her totem.

entries.name: Cave Druid
entries.description: A few druids seek to preserve the hidden underdark and purge it of the fell horrors that creep up from below.

entries.name: Death Druid
entries.description: Some druids believe that birth and death are the most important parts of the natural cycle.

entries.name: Defender of the True World
entries.description: Some druids specialize in protecting the world from the threat of First World inhabitants.

entries.name: Desert Druid
entries.description: Desert druids come to the desert to pay homage, protect and maintain the few habitable locales, and witness nature's majesty in all its burning, merciless glory.

entries.name: Devolutionist
entries.description: Devolutionists believe that the world would be better off without any sentient life at all.

entries.name: Dinosaur Druid
entries.description: A dinosaur druid speaks for the spirit of prehistoric nature, even taking the form of great beasts of legend.

entries.name: Draconic Druid
entries.description: Some druids believe that dragons are the ultimate expression of nature and eventually transform into draconic forms.

entries.name: Dragon Shaman
entries.description: Your totem is the legendary dragon, fearsome and deadly yet cunning and wise, a creature born of pure magic and raw elemental fury, bound within a shell of fangs, claws, and scales that few dare to challenge.

entries.name: Drovier
entries.description: Droviers view their allies and adventuring companions as a herd or pack to be protected and directed.

entries.name: Eagle Shaman
entries.description: A shaman with this totem calls upon the noble eagle, stern and proud, soaring high above the world with keen and pitiless eyes that miss nothing.

entries.name: Elemental Ally
entries.description: An elemental ally is a druid who has crafted powerful bonds of trust and friendship with one ally from each of the four primary elemental planes.

entries.name: Feral Child
entries.description: Some youths, abandoned in the wilderness and then raised by animals, are so connected with their adoptive home and family that they become feral.

entries.name: Feral Shifter
entries.description: A feral shifter internalizes her communion with and mastery over animals. Instead of forming a bond with an animal companion or an aspect of nature, she alters her own essence or being as homage to the noble creatures of the wild.

entries.name: Feyspeaker
entries.description: Some druids hear the whispers of the natural world like fey creatures do, and learn to mimic those tantalizing murmurs in order to influence the minds of both wild beasts and civilized people.

entries.name: Fungal Pilgrim
entries.description: Fungal pilgrims are druids seeking transformation into a more plantlike existence.

entries.name: Goliath Druid
entries.description: Goliath druids hone their spiritual and magical connections to nature’s largest creatures, especially dinosaurs, giants, and megafauna, revering these massive creatures as living relics of a primeval time when all creatures were more in harmony with nature.

entries.name: Green Faith Initiate
entries.description: Druids who are initiated into the magic of nature as strict students of the Green Faith’s traditions sometimes demonstrate abilities unique to their organization.

entries.name: Green Scourge
entries.description: Green scourges are militant druids sworn to restore natural order.

entries.name: Halcyon Druid
entries.description: Though they revere the natural world, halcyon druids are less focused on emulating its inhabitants. Instead, like Old-Mage Jatembe, they treat with beings from the Outer Sphere.

entries.name: Jungle Druid
entries.description: The jungle druid waches over the fecund jungles of the equatorial regions, rich in life and ancient tradition.

entries.name: Kraken Caller
entries.description: Some druids draw upon power irreverently stolen from one of the most dangerous creatures of the depths: the kraken.

entries.name: Leshy Warden
entries.description: The natural world is full of bodiless nature spirits connected to the forces of glades, springs, and individual plants. Some druids hear their call keenly and are able to effortlessly incarnate them as the miniature creatures known as leshys.

entries.name: Life Channeler
entries.description: By sacrificing the life of a sentient creature, life channelers can generate energy that guarantees fertility and prosperity for lower creatures like plants and animals.

entries.name: Lion Shaman
entries.description: A shaman with this totem calls upon the proud lion, imposing and majestic, the mighty leader of deadly hunters.

entries.name: Mantella
entries.description: (Grippli) A mantella focuses on exploring her poisonous heritage, whether or not it has manifested in her own personal biology.

entries.name: Menhir Savant
entries.description: Some druids study the paths of nature’s power through the nodes and ley lines that connect standing stones and megalithic circles, learning to tap into their energies.

entries.name: Mooncaller
entries.description: A mooncaller is bound to the subtle influences of the ever-changing moon and its endless cycles from light to dark and back again.

entries.name: Mountain Druid
entries.description: As more and more of the soft, easy lands become cultivated and civilized, many druids look for refuge and solitude among the eternal peaks of the highest mountains.

entries.name: Naga Aspirant
entries.description: The naga aspirant follows the ancient beliefs and engages in the rituals of a druidic sect dedicated to the transcendence of her nagaji form through absolute devotion to nagas and naga gods.

entries.name: Nature Fang
entries.description: A nature fang is a druid who stalks and slays those who despoil nature, kill scarce animals, or introduce diseases to unprotected habitats.

entries.name: Nature Priest
entries.description: Nature priests serve two masters: their deities and nature itself, and can call upon the power of both to fuel their divine abilities.

entries.name: Nithveil Adept
entries.description: Nithveil adepts learn the secret magic of the First World fey in the moving, reality-phasing city of Nithveil

entries.name: Pack Lord
entries.description: Some druids bond with many animal companions rather than just one, achieving a level of communion rare even in druidic circles and leading their pack brothers and pack sisters with total authority.

entries.name: Plains Druid
entries.description: Out upon the wide and rolling prairies and savannahs, plains druids stand guard over the grasslands.

entries.name: Planar Extremist
entries.description: (Ex-druid archetype) Planar extremists are those druids that have lost their neutral stance and find themselves gravitating toward one of the four most extreme alignments

entries.name: Progenitor
entries.description: Progenitors are druids who tap into the vibrant power of the First World to propagate natural and supernatural wonders.

entries.name: Reincarnated Druid
entries.description: Spun off into the endless circle of life, an incarnate druid is an embodiment of nature’s eternal renewal.

entries.name: Restorer
entries.description: Restorers carefully tend to the health of both the environment and creatures in it.

entries.name: River Druid
entries.description: These druids are the guardians of rivers and the creatures that depend on them.

entries.name: Road Keeper
entries.description: Guardians of the lonely paths between cities, road keepers protect the wild from travelers, and travelers from the wild.

entries.name: Rot Warden
entries.description: Harbingers of decay, rot wardens live in damp lands where insects and rot break down the dead to feed the living.

entries.name: Saurian Shaman
entries.description: A shaman with this focus calls upon the primeval dinosaur, the archaic terror that lingers as a hungering, atavistic stranger at the fringes of the ecosystem, a destroyer and despoiler whose coming other animals dread.

entries.name: Season Keeper
entries.description: Imbued with the primeval potency of their planet’s seasons, those druids known as season keepers guide Triaxian communities through the stark transition from summer to winter (and vice versa).

entries.name: Season Sage
entries.description: (Gathlain) Season sages wander as the seasons change, turning the leaves and transforming nature as they pass and taking pleasure in the transition between seasons.

entries.name: Serpent Shaman
entries.description: A shaman with this totem calls upon the cunning serpent, the stealthy deceiver who draws the weak minded in and strikes while they are unaware.

entries.name: Shark Shaman
entries.description: Some druids emulate the deadly shark, a remorseless hunter that marine dwellers dread.

entries.name: Skinshaper
entries.description: Using the same primal energy with which other druids assume animal forms, skinshapers can imitate some of the most dangerous beasts of all: humans and other humanoids.

entries.name: Sky Druid
entries.description: Some druids develop ties not to a particular landscape, but instead to the endless blue expanse of the skies.

entries.name: Storm Druid
entries.description: While most druids focus their attention upon the rich earth and the bounty of nature that springs forth from it, the storm druid’s eyes have ever been cast to the skies and the endless expanse of blue, channeling the most raw and untamed aspects of nature.

entries.name: Sunrider
entries.description: Sunriders help their allies, be they fellow tribe members or fellow adventurers, to survive in harsh desert terrain, while simultaneously making it even harsher for their foes.

entries.name: Supernaturalist
entries.description: Supernaturalists wholly embrace paranormal phenomena as extensions of nature.

entries.name: Survivor
entries.description: The survivor embodies the neutral aspect of the natural world and eschews druidic magic in favor of more pragmatic and worldly survival methods.

entries.name: Swamp Druid
entries.description: Some druids eschew pleasant glades and groves and instead seek out dank marshes, misty bogs and heaths, and trackless swamps as the place they call home and watch over with care, finding beauty and life in abundance in places few others would willingly enter.

entries.name: Swarm Monger
entries.description: Whereas other druids commune with nature or even the spirit of a city, swarm mongers find beauty and strength in decay, and they draw their power from fungus, disease, and their own singular will to survive.

entries.name: Tempest Druid
entries.description: Some druids have come to worship the Eye of Abendego as an aspect of pure elemental fury, channeling its mysteries into their own magic

entries.name: Tempest Tamer
entries.description: Tempest Tamer Source Blood of the Sea pg. 25 Druids draw upon the fiercest powers of nature, and tsunamis, typhoons, and whirlpools are among the most powerful forces in the ocean.

entries.name: Toxicologist
entries.description: Toxicologists specialize in the stealthy application of insidious poisons to their targets, believing word of their foes’ horrifying deaths will deter others from attempting similar desecrations of the natural world.

entries.name: Treesinger
entries.description: Some elves turn to the timeless growth of nature for solace, finding allies among the great trees themselves, and even leading the forest’s plants into combat.

entries.name: Troll Fury
entries.description: Troll furies combine a druid’s love of natural balance with a single-minded devotion to the welfare of the troll tribe.

entries.name: Undine Adept
entries.description: An undine adept dedicates herself to preserving the knowledge of the first undines and ensuring her people’s ancient connections to the natural world remain undisturbed.

entries.name: Urban Druid
entries.description: While many druids keep to the wilderness, some make their way within settlements, communing with the animals and vermin who live there and speaking for the nature that runs rampant in civilization's very cradle.

entries.name: Urushiol
entries.description: When an urushiol druid forms a bond with nature, it takes a vastly different form than for most druids. His body becomes increasingly toxic, allowing him to secrete a deadly poison through his pores.

entries.name: Wild Whisperer
entries.description: A wild whisperer is an expert at studying, predicting, and explaining animal behavior.

entries.name: Wolf Shaman
entries.description: A shaman with this totem calls upon the clever wolf, capable of roaming alone yet wise enough to run with a pack when facing dangers too great for one alone.

entries.name: World Walker
entries.description: While all druids traverse the wilderness with ease, the world walkers take it upon themselves to travel the entire world.

entries.name: Aerial Assaulter
entries.description: Aerial assaulters leap to great heights and create higher ground where there is none.

replaces: 2nd, 12th-level Bonus Feat, Armor Mastery, Weapon Mastery

entries.name: Airborne Ambusher
entries.description: Driven by suspicion and hatred, strix doggedly guard their territories, making deadly use of their flight.

entries.name: Aquanaut
entries.description: Aquanaut fighters master the movement of water, using its flow to their advantage in combat.

entries.name: Archer
entries.description: The archer is dedicated to the careful mastery of the bow, perfecting his skills with years of practice.

entries.name: Armiger
entries.description: Fighters who focus their training to become Hellknights.

entries.name: Armor Master
entries.description: While many fighters hone their weapon skills to a point of inescapable grace and lethality, there are those who live under the maxim that a good offense can be accomplished though an impenetrable defense.

entries.name: Brawler
entries.description: All melee is up close and personal, but some warriors bring it as close as they can get.

entries.name: Cad
entries.description: In combat, most fighters have some sort of code of honor. Some believe that one should not kick enemies when they are down, or should limit use of other such dirty tricks to the most dire of circumstances. The cad places no such limitations on himself.

entries.name: Calistrian Hunter
entries.description: Like a bounty hunter following his own rules, a Calistrian hunter tracks down elusive prey using his wits and delivers long-overdue retribution while easily ignoring his own injuries thanks to the joy he receives from a job well done.

entries.name: Cavern Sniper
entries.description: Perfectly at home in the darkness, the cavern sniper capitalizes on stealth and ranged attacks imbued with his spell-like abilities to harass his opponents.

entries.name: Child of Acavna and Amaznen
entries.description: The child of Acavna and Amaznen has trained in the nearly forgotten arts of a lost empire passed down by a dead god, which combine martial prowess with elementary wizardry. Inspired by the deities a dead god once worshiped long ago, children of Acavna and Amaznen strive to understand the dangers of the world and overcome them with knowledge and strength of arms.

entries.name: Corsair
entries.description: A corsair is a pirate who focuses on shipboard combat, relying on his strength of arms over his agility.

entries.name: Crossbowman
entries.description: The crossbowman has perfected the deadly use of the crossbow, a simple but cruelly efficient weapon, as a craftsman mastering a lethal tool.

entries.name: Cyber-Soldier
entries.description: Cyber-soldiers replace fallible flesh with precisioncrafted machinery.

entries.name: Dirty Fighter
entries.description: The dirty fighter laughs at concepts like honor and fair play. He cares only for victory, no matter how he achieves it, and spends as much time mastering sneaky combat maneuvers as he does drilling with weapons or learning how to wear armor.

entries.name: Dragonheir Scion
entries.description: Dragonheir scions are the martially inclined humanoid descendants of those influenced by draconic power.

entries.name: Dragoon
entries.description: These gallant lancers serve in the vanguard of many armies or as knights-errant.

entries.name: Drill Sergeant
entries.description: Drill sergeants excel at training other combatants in fighting techniques.

entries.name: Druman Blackjacket
entries.description: Known as the Blackjackets, the elite soldiers of a merchant principality are and always have been mercenaries rather than a standing army.

entries.name: Eldritch Guardian
entries.description: Eldritch guardians are trained to detect and give warning about magic threats to the people and places they protect.

entries.name: Foehammer
entries.description: While the axe is the most famous dwarven weapon, the hammer is at the heart of dwarves’ heritage as forgemasters and warriors alike.

entries.name: Free Hand Fighter
entries.description: The free hand fighter specializes in the delicate art of handling a single weapon in one hand while using his free hand to balance, block, tip, and distract his opponents.

entries.name: Gladiator
entries.description: The gladiator is both a cunning warrior and a consummate performer, knowing life and death are balanced not only on a sword’s edge, but also on the cheers or jeers of the crowd.

entries.name: Gloomblade
entries.description: The Shadow Plane’s substance is legendary for its versatility. In shadow-shrouded lands, secretive martial practitioners long ago learned to shape supernatural weapons from ribbons of pure darkness.

entries.name: High Guardian
entries.description: High guardians epitomize personal devotion, serving as the shield that protects his lord from the myriad dangers around every corner.

entries.name: Lore Warden
entries.description: Lore wardens are fighters who benefit from learning to outsmart and outmaneuver their foes rather than just overpower them.

entries.name: Lore Warden (PFS Field Guide)
entries.description: Lore wardens are fighters who benefit from learning to outsmart and outmaneuver their foes rather than just overpower them.

replaces: Medium Armor, Heavy Armor, and Shield Proficiency

entries.name: Martial Master
entries.description: There are those who learn the fighting arts though countless hours of repetition and training, while others seem to pick up new stances and forms as if they were born to them.

entries.name: Mobile Fighter
entries.description: Where some fighters focus on strength and raw power, the mobile fighter relies on swiftness and mobility, gliding across the battlefield like a steel whirlwind and leaving destruction in his wake.

entries.name: Molthuni Defender
entries.description: Taking advantage of their weighty armor, Molthuni defenders can hold back an onslaught of enemies intent on breaking through their line.

entries.name: Mutation Warrior
entries.description: While most fighters rely on physical fitness and rigorous training to achieve martial superiority, a few prefer to create and imbibe dangerous concoctions that mutate them into fearsome creatures.

entries.name: Opportunist
entries.description: Opportunists believe every battle is one of wits rather than arms.

entries.name: Pack Mule
entries.description: Pack mules carry heavy loads with ease and small packages with discretion.

entries.name: Phalanx Soldier
entries.description: The phalanx soldier specializes in defensive tactics, using his shield to guard himself and his allies and forming a shield wall like an unbreakable anvil against which his enemies break.

entries.name: Polearm Master
entries.description: The polearm master is schooled in the ancient wisdom that enemies are best faced at the end of long striking pole.

entries.name: Relic Master
entries.description: Commonly trained in the well-funded temples of an ancient desert kingdom or a desert kingdom, the relic master is skilled in magic item mastery.

entries.name: Roughrider
entries.description: Roughriders study and practice the fine points of mounted combat, drilling endlessly with warbeasts—from noble thoroughbreds to trained monsters—to form a perfect synergy between rider and steed.

entries.name: Savage Warrior
entries.description: Warriors' might is not measured only by their skill with steel, but also by their ability to inflict death with fang and claw, horn and hoof, and every exotic appendage the natural and unnatural world has to offer.

entries.name: Scrapper
entries.description: Scrappers are adept at collecting the leftovers from their enemy’s armor and using these scraps to improve their own armor.

entries.name: Seasoned Commander
entries.description: The seasoned commander excels at leading troops through inspiration and the use of unit tactics.

entries.name: Sensate
entries.description: A sensate perceives battle through senses beyond mortal ken, anticipating his opponents’ movements before they even begin to act.

entries.name: Shielded Fighter
entries.description: A shielded fighter focuses on both offense and defense, blending weapon and shield in perfect balance to impede his enemies while delivering deadly blows, and even turning the shield itself into a formidable weapon.

entries.name: Siegebreaker
entries.description: The siegebreaker is trained to break through lines of enemy soldiers.

entries.name: Skirmisher
entries.description: Not all battles are fought between armies; sometimes, a settlement or nation faces a threat too dire to fight in the open. In order to repel a much larger enemy force, some soldiers must abandon equipment and tactics designed for open-field warfare and instead rely on ambushes, hit-andrun tactics, and sabotage to whittle down their enemies’ strength and morale.

entries.name: Spear Fighter
entries.description: One of the oldest spear-fighting styles originates in a distant continent, where many martial arts traditions consider the spear to be the ultimate weapon.

entries.name: Steelbound Fighter
entries.description: A fighter who has impressive martial resolve and technique with a specific weapon as the result of a powerful relationship a similar weapon had with one of his ancestors.

entries.name: Swarm Fighter
entries.description: Scuttling between the legs of friend and foe alike, the swarm fighter is an unshakable combatant.

entries.name: Tactician
entries.description: While many fighters focus on the fundamentals of melee and ranged combat, there are those who are trained to view the bigger picture on the battlefield.

entries.name: Thunderstriker
entries.description: The thunderstriker adopts an unusual fighting style, gripping a heavy weapon with both hands and switching to a defensive posture with weapon and buckler, lashing out with the shield with surprising speed and power.

entries.name: Titan Fighter
entries.description: Titan fighters make use of enormous weapons others can barely lift.

entries.name: Tower Shield Specialist
entries.description: Many fighters believe the tower shield is a tool suitable only for troops on the battlefield, claiming it is too large and bulky to use in skirmishes or within dungeon corridors.

entries.name: Trench Fighter
entries.description: Advances in technology have made archaic armors obsolete by the twentieth century, and modern soldiers concentrate training on firearms and swift feet.

entries.name: Tribal Fighter
entries.description: A tribal fighter knows that it is not the weapon that matters but the hand that wields it. Instead of encasing himself in metal armor like the soldiers fighting and dying for the socalled civilized lands do, he prefers to wear something he or his ancestors have killed.

entries.name: Two-Handed Fighter
entries.description: Some fighters focus their efforts on finding the biggest, heaviest, most imposing weapon they can find and training to manage and harness the weight of their massive weapons for maximum impact.

entries.name: Two-Weapon Warrior
entries.description: Trained under great masters who preached the simple truth that two are better than one when it comes to weapons, the two-weapon warrior is a terror when his hands are full.

entries.name: Unarmed Fighter
entries.description: The unarmed fighter picks up a weapon only rarely, and when he does, he prefers the weapons of the monk.

entries.name: Unbreakable
entries.description: The unbreakable is a warrior of indomitable will, unstoppable and implacable once he has set his mind upon a course of action.

entries.name: Ustalavic Duelist
entries.description: The University of Lepidstadt has developed a reputation for churning out fearsome duelists. At the end of each academic year, the students all gather together and duel one another with light blades. Each student duels one opponent after another until he is marked on the cheek by an adversary’s blade. These “Lepidstadt scars” are recognized throughout the inner sea region and beyond as marks of their prowess. The Lepidstadt Style is one of fluid motion and precise thrusts.

entries.name: Venomblade
entries.description: (Nagaji) The venomblade has learned to take full advantage of his toxic spittle, blinding his targets and then rushing in to cut them down where they stand.

entries.name: Viking
entries.description: Vikings seek to raid “softer societies” and return with their longships filled with plunder. A viking strikes fear into the heart of her foes, and in battle she can fly into a terrible rage.

entries.name: Warlord
entries.description: Honorable, fearless experts in gun and blade, warlords eschew armor as impractical to their harsh and often desert-like environment

entries.name: Weapon Bearer Squire
entries.description: The weapon bearer squire ensures her knight is equipped for any task.

entries.name: Weapon Master
entries.description: Devoted to the perfection of a single weapon, the weapon master's meditations upon his favored weapon border on the obsessive, but none can deny his consummate skill.

entries.name: Black Asp
entries.description: The black asps are a sinister order of monks who train as assassins and infiltrators with no need for weapons to achieve their goals.

entries.name: Brazen Disciple
entries.description: Brazen disciples use deception in their fighting style, and many go a step further, incorporating fire and smoke both mundane and magical.

entries.name: Disciple of Wholeness
entries.description: Disciples of wholeness train to bring themselves and others closer to physical and spiritual perfection.

entries.name: Drunken Master
entries.description: The drunken master finds perfection through excess.

entries.name: Elemental Monk
entries.description: Elemental monks draw inspiration from genies to create their fighting style. Their adaptability and versatility make them capable of serving as emissaries of elemental balance.

entries.name: Far Strike Monk
entries.description: Far strike monks are masters of thrown weapons, from shuriken to throwing axes to spears.

entries.name: Flowing Monk
entries.description: The flowing monk is the wind and the river. He knows how the world flows, and forces his enemies to flow with it.

entries.name: Gray Disciple
entries.description: The gray disciple contemplates the inner voice of duergar magic and the silent eternity of stone, mastering these dual mysteries and combining them to deadly effect.

replaces: Tongue of the Sun and Moon

entries.name: Hamatulatsu Master
entries.description: Once part of the Sisterhood of Eiseth, the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinyes is an order of female monks dedicated to emulating the painful strikes of the barbed devil, leaving targets alive but permanently scarred and broken by pain—a method called hamatulatsu.

entries.name: Harrow Warden
entries.description: Some who study the mysteries of the harrow do so to restore lost knowledge and pride to the frontier people. The harrow warden fulfills this role as she seeks to bring her mind and body into alignment, and she protects her people by invoking the folklore that has guided them for so long. In mastering her own place in fate, a harrow warden learns how to misalign the destinies of others.

entries.name: Hellcat
entries.description: Monks of the hellcat sect follow the teachings of a tyrant god or another infernal power.

entries.name: Hungry Ghost Monk
entries.description: The hungry ghost monk looks to spirits that prey upon the living as models of perfection.

entries.name: Invested Regent
entries.description: The invested regent can harness a divine spark to perform superhuman stunts, influence others, and escape injury.

entries.name: Ironskin Monk
entries.description: Through discipline and training, an ironskin monk hardens his body to withstand punishing blows.

replaces: Tongue of the Sun and Moon

entries.name: Karmic Monk
entries.description: A karmic monk contemplates the myriad harmonies that guide existence. He learns to use the disharmony in others against them, and to alter his own inner harmonies to exploit weaknesses in his opponents’ defenses.

entries.name: Kata Master
entries.description: The kata master takes the visual aspect of his martial art to its logical extreme, harnessing her flowing movements and skilled maneuvers as a psychological weapon against her enemies.

entries.name: Ki Mystic
entries.description: The ki mystic believes that violence is sometimes necessary, but knowing and understanding is the true root of perfection.

entries.name: Lifting Hand
entries.description: When facing a master of the lifting hand, an enemy is likely to find itself sailing through the air or locked in a tortuous compliance hold.

entries.name: Maneuver Master
entries.description: The maneuver master specializes in more complicated moves than simple damage-dealing strikes.

entries.name: Martial Artist
entries.description: The martial artist pursues a mastery of pure martial arts without the monastic traditions. He is a master of form, but lacks the ability to harness his ki.

entries.name: Master of Many Styles
entries.description: The master of many styles is a collector. For every move, he seeks a counter. For every style, he has a riposte.

entries.name: Menhir Guardian
entries.description: Menhir guardians are ascetic protectors of sacred druidic sites, less concerned with structure and maintaining internal order than they are with preserving the natural balance of the world.

entries.name: Monk of the Empty Hand
entries.description: The monk of the empty hand eschews normal weapons in favor of whatever is lying around—rocks, chair legs, flagons of ale, even a simple quill pen all become deadly weapons in the hands of such a monk.

entries.name: Monk of the Four Winds
entries.description: The monk of the four winds is connected to the natural world in a way few other creatures—even other monks—can hope to match.

entries.name: Monk of the Healing Hand
entries.description: Monks of the healing hand seek perfection through helping others.

entries.name: Monk of the Lotus
entries.description: While a monk of the lotus realizes that combat cannot always be avoided—and is more than capable in a fight—he understands that all creatures are connected, and to harm another is to harm the self.

replaces: Tongue of the Sun and the Moon

entries.name: Monk of the Mantis
entries.description: A body contains many points where the flesh, mind, and spirit coincide. A monk of the mantis is skilled at manipulating these points.

entries.name: Monk of the Sacred Mountain
entries.description: The monk of the sacred mountain finds strength and power in the earth beneath his feet.

replaces: Tongue of the Sun and the Moon

entries.name: Monk of the Seven Forms
entries.description: In their place, the monks of the isolated sanctuary now teach a style featuring lightning-fast strikes that mimic both dervish dances and the searing winds of the arid desert, favoring mobility and endurance.

entries.name: Nimble Guardian
entries.description: Some catfolk monks dedicate their graceful prowess to the defense of others, especially those dedicated to a similar ethos or who prove themselves as stalwart allies of the monk’s cause.

entries.name: Nornkith
entries.description: Nornkith hone their bodies and minds to follow the branching threefold paths of fate.

entries.name: Ouat
entries.description: The ascetic, desert-dwelling dwarves known as the Ouat have eschewed dwarven traditions, whose unchanging rigidity, they believe, shackles their people to the past and inhibits self-improvement.

replaces: Greed, Hatred, Defensive Training, Stonecunning, Weapon Familiarity (Dwarven Racial Traits)

entries.name: Perfect Scholar
entries.description: Perfect scholars, often worshipers of a god of perfection, hone their minds and bodies through the accumulation of knowledge

replaces: Tongue of the Sun and Moon

entries.name: Qinggong Monk
entries.description: The qinggong monk is a master of her ki, using it to perform superhuman stunts or even blast opponents with supernatural energy.

replaces: Tongue of the Sun and Moon

entries.name: Sage Counselor
entries.description: Sage counselors are ascetics and mystics who leave the confines of the monastery walls to advise secular people about spiritual truths and to seek knowledge of the outside world.

entries.name: Scaled Fist
entries.description: Scaled fists eschew passive introspection in favor of unshakable confidence. Steeped in traditions that trace their origins to the warrior-monks who trained under the tutelage of draconic masters in a faraway continent, scaled fists eschew passive introspection in favor of unshakable confidence. Scaled fists learn to combine brutal intimidation with the brazen ferocity of an ancient wyrm to devastate their foes.

entries.name: Scarred Monk
entries.description: For monks who seek the truth hidden in pain, the practice of mortifications of the flesh helps to achieve enlightenment and acquire disturbing powers.

entries.name: Sensei
entries.description: The sensei is a revered teacher who imparts lessons on the oneness of mind, body, and spirit, along with occasional correction that is subtle and swift.

entries.name: Serpent-Fire Adept
entries.description: A serpent-fire adept embraces the secrets of her chakras and mastery of their energetic flow.

entries.name: Sin Monk
entries.description: (Ex-monk archetype) Martial experts who have allowed such passions to lead them astray may find themselves gaining powers drawn from their newly embraced sins.

entries.name: Softstrike Monk
entries.description: Softstrike monks employ a nonlethal but effective form of combat.

entries.name: Sohei
entries.description: The sohei are masters of the horse and the hunt.

entries.name: Soul Shepherd
entries.description: Whether studying at the feet of psychopomps or merely imitating the creatures' philosophy and methods, soul shepherds believe in safeguarding the Cycle of Souls.

entries.name: Spirit Master
entries.description: Spirit masters are monks who specialize in combating the undead, laying their corpses to rest, and sending their souls to final judgment.

entries.name: Student of Stone
entries.description: By following the path of the stone, students of stone give up much of monks’ mobility in favor of sheer resilience.

entries.name: Terra-Cotta Monk
entries.description: Possessing a natural affinity for all things earthen, terracotta monks are experts at turning the stone around them against their enemies.

entries.name: Tetori
entries.description: The style of the tetori is that of the majestic wrestler—a warrior with a dizzying array of grabs, holds, and locks with which to bewilder and incapacitate his foes.

entries.name: Treetop Monk
entries.description: While many vanaras follow traditional monastic training and traditions, others learn to blend exotic combat and the mysterious forces of ki with the natural world, allowing them to move through trees and overgrowth to deliver devastating attacks.

entries.name: Underfoot Adept
entries.description: An underfoot adept turns his diminutive stature and unorthodox footwork into a powerful weapon.

entries.name: Wanderer
entries.description: Some monks wander the world in humility to learn and to share wisdom and philosophy from their teachers with those they meet, often aiding those who are in need.

entries.name: Wasteland Meditant
entries.description: Some monks journey to remote and isolated corners of the world to find serenity and a heightened sense of awareness.

entries.name: Water Dancer
entries.description: Water dancers derive their martial training from ancient nereid traditions jealously guarded by these enigmatic fey.

entries.name: Weapon Adept
entries.description: While all monks train in both unarmed combat and with weapons, the weapon adept seeks to become one with his weapons, transforming them into perfect extensions of his own body.

entries.name: Wildcat
entries.description: A wildcat is a student of the school of hard knocks, who dedicates himself to learning how to take down foes by any means necessary.

entries.name: Windstep Master
entries.description: Most monks are agile and fleet of foot, but few can rival a windstep master’s lightness of step.

entries.name: Zen Archer
entries.description: The zen archer takes a weapon most other monks eschew and seeks perfection in the pull of a taut bowstring, the flex of a bow’s limbs, and the flight of an arrow fired true.

replaces: Tongue of the Sun and the Moon

entries.name: Banishing Warden
entries.description: The banishing warden is an expert at fighting all types of evil outsiders and sending them back to their native planes.

entries.name: Champion of the Cascade
entries.description: Champions of the cascade are paladins who defend the freedom and purity of waterways, protecting the very existence of the civilizations they belong to.

entries.name: Chaos Knight
entries.description: Despite the entropic forces inherent in ganzis, some forgo a life of chaos, instead harnessing their heritage to enforce the power of law

entries.name: Chosen One
entries.description: Most paladins train for years at a temple to attain a holy status, but rarely, an emissary of the divine appears to one of humble origins and calls her directly to the charge.

entries.name: Combat Healer Squire
entries.description: The combat healer squire is always ready with bandages and potions.

entries.name: Divine Defender
entries.description: Some paladins see themselves as the last line of defense between the teeming hordes of evil and the innocent folk trying to make a living in a harsh, unforgiving world.

entries.name: Divine Guardian
entries.description: The divine guardian devotes herself to the protection and guardianship of one creature at a time, be that her liege lord, an allied cleric, or an innocent facing overwhelming danger at the hands of evil.

entries.name: Divine Hunter
entries.description: The divine hunter prefers to engage evil from afar, striking down her foes before they can threaten her allies.

entries.name: Dusk Knight
entries.description: Some paladins focus their training to combat the shadows and use darkness to their advantage.

entries.name: Empyreal Knight
entries.description: The empyreal knight dedicates her life to serving the celestial beings that guide mortals in their struggle toward the light.

entries.name: Faithful Wanderer
entries.description: A faithful wanderer is self-sufficient and unobtrusive and learns to pick her battles carefully, lest her mission end abruptly in a blaze of glory

entries.name: Forest Preserver
entries.description: Forest preservers are sacred defenders of the woodlands and of the wild creatures and natural beauty within them.

entries.name: Forgefather's Seeker
entries.description: a god of the forge sends his seekers to locate constructs that are used for evil or that become uncontrollable

entries.name: Ghost Hunter
entries.description: Ghost hunters devote their lives to eliminating malevolent spirits and putting them to rest.

entries.name: Gray Paladin
entries.description: Gray paladins have discovered that in a world of intrigue, a strict code of honor hinders their options

entries.name: Holy Guide
entries.description: A holy guide believes that it’s his sacred calling to clear the roads of bandits between towns as well as to escort travelers to safety.

entries.name: Holy Gun
entries.description: Not all paladins are knights in shining armor. Holy guns roam the world searching for evil. And where they find it, they put it down.

entries.name: Holy Tactician
entries.description: The holy tactician inspires her allies on the field of battle.

entries.name: Hospitaler
entries.description: Paladins are known for their charity and for tending to the sick. The hospitaler takes to this calling above all others, spending much of her time healing the poor, and giving aid and succor to those in need.

entries.name: Hunting Paladin
entries.description: Hunting paladins are tenacious trackers and stealthy stalkers in pursuit of evildoers.

entries.name: Invigorator
entries.description: Invigorators devote themselves to keeping their allies bodily whole by bolstering their health and spirits.

entries.name: Iomedaen Enforcer
entries.description: Iomedaean enforcers have altered abilities that allow them to stand against the forces of chaos.

entries.name: Iroran Paladin
entries.description: Iroran paladins meditate on self-perfection and train relentlessly, knowing that their example can inspire others to excel.

entries.name: Knight of Coins
entries.description: Knights of coins promote fair trade and stable commerce between cities and between nations.

entries.name: Kraken Slayer
entries.description: Triton kraken slayers oppose all underwater threats, but they especially target the tentacled monstrosities called krakens.

entries.name: Legate
entries.description: Though they hold to the same strict paladin code, legates present themselves not as armed crusaders, but as peaceful envoys and advisors, bringing wisdom garnered from the long, stable history of their nation.

entries.name: Martyr
entries.description: Martyrs shoulder the blackest suffering of the world onto themselves in order to help others and inspiring their allies to achieve heights of valor rather than seeking the glory for themselves.

entries.name: Mind Sword
entries.description: Veterans of mystical battles against demons of a demon-blighted land, mind swords merge psychic and divine power, probing and cleansing minds while their telekinetic blades cleave demonic flesh.

entries.name: Pearl Seeker
entries.description: Some paladins are called to their faith by strange empathic visions and dreams that beckon them to the oceans and beyond.

entries.name: Redeemer
entries.description: As most half-orcs are outcasts, a half-orc paladin recognizes that often those who are monstrous are not necessarily evil and that sometimes even those who are evil became that way because of circumstances and misfortune.

entries.name: Sacred Servant
entries.description: Paladins as a general rule, venerate the gods of good and purity, but some take this a step further, dedicating themselves to a specific deity and furthering the cause of the faith.

entries.name: Sacred Shield
entries.description: When faced by evil, the sacred shield reaches first not for a weapon, but for her trusty shield. With her faith, she can ward others from harm.

entries.name: Scion of Talmandor
entries.description: A scion of Talmandor serve by offering assistance to the oppressed and facilitating the peaceful transfer of power from the few to the many.

entries.name: Shining Knight
entries.description: While paladins often are seen mounted atop a loyal steed, the shining knight is the true symbol of mounted bravery.

entries.name: Silver Champion
entries.description: Drake-riding paladins who serve as priests of Apsu.

entries.name: Soul Sentinel
entries.description: Soul sentinels use the strength of their resolve to stem the tide of corruption and insanity, as they believe that the greatest tragedy is a soul lost to evil when it was within their power to save it.

entries.name: Stonelord
entries.description: A stonelord is a devoted sentinel of dwarven enclaves, drawing the power of the earth and ancient stone to protect her people.

entries.name: Sword of Valor
entries.description: A paladin who chooses to follow in a goddess of valor's footsteps can become a sword of valor.

entries.name: Tempered Champion
entries.description: Tempered champions are trained in the Tempering Hall in a great city to master their deities’ favored weapons.

entries.name: Temple Champion
entries.description: A temple champion is a powerful warrior dedicated to a good or lawful deity. She thinks of herself primarily as a servant of her deity and secondarily as an agent of her deity’s church.

entries.name: Tortured Crusader
entries.description: Though tortured crusaders may be beaten and battered, body, mind, and soul, they still somehow continue through torment and hardship. Despite setbacks and impossible odds, they shine like candles even in the darkest times

entries.name: Tranquil Guardian
entries.description: A tranquil guardian is a missionary of peace and tranquility, a soothing voice of succor in a violent and dangerous world.

entries.name: Undead Scourge
entries.description: Undead are an abomination in the eyes of the just and righteous. It is no surprise then that there are some paladins that dedicate themselves to wiping these unholy terrors from the world.

entries.name: Vindictive Bastard
entries.description: (Ex-paladin archetype) A vindictive bastard is a paladin that strikes out for retribution and revenge, far more interested in tearing down those who have harmed her or her companions than furthering a distant deity’s cause.

entries.name: Virtuous Bravo
entries.description: Virtuous bravos rely on their wit and grace rather than might and strong armor.

entries.name: Warrior of the Holy Light
entries.description: Some paladins use their gifts to focus on the holy light that shines within their souls.

entries.name: Wilderness Warden
entries.description: Wilderness wardens are vigilant guardians of natural places of all kinds, from mountain peaks to tangled thickets.

entries.name: Abendego Diver
entries.description: Named for the vicious and unending storm in the southern Arcadian Ocean, Abendego divers have pushed their bodies to their limits, holding their breath to expand their lung capacity and swimming until ocean travel is second nature to them.

entries.name: Battle Scout
entries.description: Though regular outdoorsmen might suffice in many cases, some large forces look to battle scouts to keep the body of their troops safe and prepared for the terrain and whatever dangers that terrain hides.

entries.name: Beast Master
entries.description: Some rangers, particularly those in primitive lands or who were raised by animals, have unusually strong bonds with animals.

entries.name: Blightwarden
entries.description: Some rangers feel so closely connected to their homelands that they stand as guardians against pervasive corruptions that pervert those lands beyond the point of recognition.

entries.name: Bow Nomad
entries.description: Thanks to their four arms, kasathas can master a combat form native to their home world and rarely witnessed on the world—wielding two bows at once.

entries.name: Cinderwalker
entries.description: Cinderwalkers traverse burning wastelands and restless mountains, thriving in lands most creatures avoid.

entries.name: Code Runner
entries.description: A code runner specializes in the subtle and speedy transfer of secret messages.

entries.name: Corpse Hunter
entries.description: Many rangers count the undead among their favored enemies, but some make a full-time job out of hunting down and destroying these walking corpses.

entries.name: Dandy
entries.description: The antithesis of the gruff and wild woodsmen, a dandy takes effort to master the subtle etiquette of noble courts, the whispers of dark rumors, and the customs of the cultured world.

entries.name: Darklands Sailor
entries.description: Those plying the lightless waters of the Darklands learn to use sound to augment their compromised vision, providing insight into the hazards lurking below the surface.

entries.name: Deep Walker
entries.description: Some rangers devote their lives to the woods, becoming hunters, protectors, and wilderness guides among its diverse terrain types.

entries.name: Divine Tracker
entries.description: Blessed by his deity, a divine tracker hunts down those he deems deserving of his retribution.

entries.name: Dragon Hunter
entries.description: The quintessential dragonslayers, dragon hunters are experts at forging through the wilds in search of great wyrms.

entries.name: Drake Warden
entries.description: Some rangers specialize in dealing with rambunctious younger drakes and thanks to their methods, their drakes are both fiercely loyal and extremely useful for scouting and stealth missions.

entries.name: Dungeon Rover
entries.description: These rangers specialize in surviving hostile subterranean environs. They are well equipped to avoid traps, spot secret passages, and deal with inimical dungeon tenants.

entries.name: Dusk Stalker
entries.description: Hunters and guides through the Shadow Plane, dusk stalkers are rangers that thrive in shadow.

entries.name: Elemental Envoy
entries.description: An elemental envoy travels the Elemental Planes. He has learned to protect himself from their many dangers, and he models his fighting style after their teachings.

entries.name: Falconer
entries.description: Rangers have always enjoyed a special bond with a specific animal, but the falconer takes this bond to a deeper level.

entries.name: Flamewarden
entries.description: Emulating the blazing phoenix, flamewardens sweep through the world like a selective forest fire, burning away corruption, evil, and those who cling to decay.

entries.name: Fortune-Finder
