entries.description: Vanaras often leave home to seek fortune and sate their curiosity regarding the mysterious lands that lie beyond their native territories. The most skilled of these thrillseekers are called ba-sadhaks, or fortune-finders.

entries.name: Freebooter
entries.description: A freebooter is a natural leader, a pirate who works well with a variety of people and in a variety of roles.

entries.name: Galvanic Saboteur
entries.description: Many northern tribal locals blame Kevoth-Kul’s change on the influence of the Technic League and view both the League and their mechanical minions with a mix of fear and distrust. Some northern tribal rangers have since developed skills to defeat the League’s robotic enforcers and devious arcanists.

entries.name: Groom
entries.description: The groom attends to the needs of the party’s mounts and beasts of burden during their adventures, and guards these animals while the party goes underground.

entries.name: Guide
entries.description: Many rangers are loners, but some choose to use their familiarity with the land to guide others safely through the wilderness.

entries.name: Guildbreaker
entries.description: Guildbreakers stoke their enmity for their foes, and they train to track the movements of rival organizations, and even to infiltrate these groups to gather secret intelligence.

entries.name: Hooded Champion
entries.description: The hooded champion lives on the periphery of civilized lands, and is often at odds with the forces of law and order.

entries.name: Horse Lord
entries.description: Rangers of the plains use horses or other riding beasts to hunt their lands, forging a near-mystical relationship with their mounts.

entries.name: Ilsurian Archer
entries.description: Ilsurian archers maintain the strong tradition of archery first developed by soldiers in the service of Ilsur, who raised a small army with which he intended to overthrow the monarch of a port city after the fall of the diabolic Empire.

entries.name: Infiltrator
entries.description: Some rangers study their favored enemies and learn their ways, applying this knowledge to their own abilities and using their foes’ strengths against them.

entries.name: Jungle Lord
entries.description: Jungle lords are tempered by their harsh and unforgiving environments into something more than ordinary men and women.

entries.name: Lantern Lighter
entries.description: Lantern lighters were originally entrusted with secretly eliminating the drow and quarantining any knowledge of their existence, but in the new Lantern Bearer era, the lantern lighters have refocused their efforts on helping to rescue those imprisoned by the drow, or even to help individual drow who seek to escape the cruelties of their society for a chance at redemption on the surface.

entries.name: Nirmathi Irregular
entries.description: An irregular troop from a rebel nation, this ranger chooses to focus on the magic of stealth.

entries.name: Planar Scout
entries.description: Planar scouts are rangers specializing in traversing the planes—and surviving their journeys.

entries.name: Poison Darter
entries.description: In dense jungles, foliage and tight spaces hinder all but the most deceptively humble weapons: blowguns and poison.

entries.name: Raven Master
entries.description: Raven masters serve as messengers and spies for the Silver Ravens, eschewing a ranger’s usual connection to the natural world to form a mystic bond with their birds and to grant both animal and master a number of specialized abilities

entries.name: Realm Wanderer
entries.description: These rangers take to heart the lessons they’ve learned from their vastly contrasting experiences and know that creatively embracing this wisdom is sometimes the difference between life and death.

entries.name: Sable Company Marine
entries.description: Sable Company marines receive their training at the elite Endrin Military Academy in a port city. A large portion of their education is the handling and riding of hippogriffs, the iconic mounts of members of the company.

entries.name: Sentinel
entries.description: A sentinel specializes in heightening all of her senses to expose spies and those who work for opposing factions, rooting out all who attempt to slip past her evervigilant watch.

entries.name: Shapeshifter
entries.description: Most rangers venture into the wilderness, but there are some who let the wilderness seep into them.

entries.name: Skirmisher
entries.description: Many rangers rely on spells, but there are some who eschew aid from divine powers for their own reasons.

entries.name: Spirit Ranger
entries.description: Some rangers nurture a connection with the spirits that reside in all things.

entries.name: Stormwalker
entries.description: Rangers who walk in the tempest unafraid draw the power of the storm into themselves and become stormwalkers.

entries.name: Summit Sentinel
entries.description: Some rangers eschew the path of the swift skirmisher and embrace the implacable strength of the mountain.

entries.name: Sword-Devil
entries.description: Agile, vengeful, and deadly, a sword-devil ﬁghts with precision and grace, channeling the difficult lessons of a star-crossed life into unparalleled battle prowess.

entries.name: Tanglebriar Demonslayer
entries.description: Though they are sworn foes of Treerazer and his kin, Tanglebriar demonslayers are known to venture forth from an elven realm to broaden their expertise in the destruction of demons.

entries.name: Tidal Hunter
entries.description: The tidal hunter draws strength from the fish and other wildlife of the deep.

entries.name: Toxic Herbalist
entries.description: Saviors and destroyers in equal measure, toxic herbalists use nature’s bounty to craft remedies and poisons.

entries.name: Toxophilite
entries.description: The toxophilite emulates the sharpshooting rangers of legend, who could pin a fly to the wall with a single shot or split one arrow with another.

entries.name: Transporter
entries.description: Transporters specialize in smuggling people as efficiently as possible through harsh and difficult environments.

entries.name: Trapper
entries.description: A trapper is a ranger who focuses exclusively on traps, rather than learning conventional magic.

entries.name: Trophy Hunter
entries.description: Some rangers have taken up the mysteries of black powder in order to become big game hunters.

entries.name: Urban Ranger
entries.description: For the urban ranger, the streets and sewers of the city are just as dangerous as the barren wastelands or the deep forests.

entries.name: Warden
entries.description: All rangers have a bond with the wilderness, but the warden may have the strongest. This protector sits guard in the middle of the wilderness, keeping a lookout for any dangers that might spill from the deeper wilderness beyond, and protecting civilization from the savagery of nature—and vice versa.

entries.name: Wave Warden
entries.description: The wave warden patrols beneath the sea, preserving the safety and secrets of merfolk communities.

entries.name: Wild Hunter
entries.description: A wild hunter seeks to emulate the animals around him to keep him safe while he tracks his prey.

entries.name: Wild Shadow
entries.description: The isolation that some half-elves feel leads them to live a life of isolation amid the wild places of the world.

entries.name: Wild Soul
entries.description: Wild souls hail from primitive roots in the wild and venture to more civilized lands and learn their ways.

entries.name: Wild Stalker
entries.description: The wild stalker forsakes the bonds of community and lives in the trackless wilds far from others of his kind, or perhaps grew up there, never knowing of civilization as anything more than his enemy.

entries.name: Wilderness Explorer
entries.description: Wilderness explorers are adept at making peaceful contact with remote societies.

entries.name: Wilderness Medic
entries.description: Wilderness medics know a variety of ways they can supply and preserve a rebellion or similar movement without requiring any resources that might make them easier to track down.

entries.name: Witchguard
entries.description: Witchguards are the sworn defenders of the White Witches of a winter-locked realm.

entries.name: Yokai Hunter
entries.description: Yokai hunters possess a supernatural tether to the spirit worlds that shroud mortal existence.

entries.name: Acrobat
entries.description: Whether they are daring thieves, infiltrating assassins, or intrepid spies, proper training in acrobatics is a valuable boon for rogues.

entries.name: Bandit
entries.description: Bandits tend to have a variety of skills; sometimes these skills are similar to a ranger’s, but a bandit’s tactics always deal with surprise followed by intimidation, with the clear threat of naked force if intimidation does not do the trick.

entries.name: Bekyar Kidnapper
entries.description: A Bekyar kidnapper is not only adept at hiding herself in thick jungles and quickly subduing her prey, but also at spreading rumors of hidden ruins, buried treasure, and other such valuables that might lure an unwary foreigner into her traps.

entries.name: Bellflower Irrigator
entries.description: Rather than focusing on saving slaves, Bellflower irrigators seek to defeat slavery by aiming to eliminate the source.

entries.name: Burglar
entries.description: Adept at infiltration, trap removal, and lock picking, burglars prey on the homes of the wealthy and forgotten tombs alike.

entries.name: Carnivalist
entries.description: Carnivalists train their miniature minions to perform acts of larceny and often hide their true talents behind theatrical sideshows.

entries.name: Cat Burglar
entries.description: Cat burglars are masters of breaking and entering, using their feline grace to make it seem as though no crime was ever committed in the first place.

entries.name: Chameleon
entries.description: An absolute master of disguise, a chameleon effortlessly blends into any environment.

entries.name: Charlatan
entries.description: A charlatan is a master of lies and deception.

entries.name: Consigliere
entries.description: Consiglieres act as trusted mediators and administrators for crime families and various criminal organizations, and many serve as the right hand to the leaders of such groups.

entries.name: Construct Saboteur
entries.description: The construct saboteur harnesses arcane energy to combat the golems and eldritch guardians that prowl the depths of ancient ruins and forgotten tombs.

entries.name: Counterfeit Mage
entries.description: Charlatans and stage magicians use slight of hand to fake magic. A counterfeit mage goes a step further, parroting the motions and activation phrases used by arcane casters to activate wands or other magical accoutrements.

entries.name: Cutpurse
entries.description: Cutpurses are often trained by guilds to collect the guild’s tax from local businesses on a daily basis, whether through intimidation or pickpocketing. Some find themselves taking up the mantle of adventurer, and their talents are generally appreciated in this role, but the cutpurse is still the first person her companions look to when an item goes missing.

entries.name: Dark Lurker
entries.description: Dark lurkers use darkness as an ally.

entries.name: Deadly Courtesan
entries.description: Skilled at manipulation and diversion, the deadly courtesan builds up those around her and periodically takes them down.

entries.name: Desert Raider
entries.description: Desert raider learn the secrets of the deserts and become inured to their dangers.

entries.name: Discretion Specialist
entries.description: Discretion specialists deal with bodies, inconvenient witnesses, and other loose ends.

entries.name: Dreamthief
entries.description: Each dreamthief bears a focused fragment of emotion, known as a dreamshard, within her soul. This metaphysical crystal grants a dreamthief supernatural powers, which she supplements with skill and grace.

entries.name: Driver
entries.description: A driver makes her living driving vehicles in the service of those who can pay for her considerable talents.

entries.name: Earthshadow
entries.description: In the centuries since the Quest for the Sky, the mystic lore the dwarves call earthcraft has been passed down through the generations, and its practitioners are called earthshadows.

entries.name: Eldritch Raider
entries.description: An eldritch raider is a rogue who seeks to unravel the mysteries of the destruction of the gillmen’s homeland.

entries.name: Eldritch Scoundrel
entries.description: Students of arcane magic, legerdemain, and stealth, eldritch scoundrels are a rare breed of adventurer most commonly found seeking lost and valuable arcane writings in the ruins of fallen empires, such as an ancient empire or the Jistka Imperium.

entries.name: Escapologist
entries.description: The escapologist excels at escaping any confinement, whether physical, magical, or mental. Few restraints can hold an escapologist for long.

entries.name: False Medium
entries.description: The false medium is a master of pretending to have occult powers in order to manipulate the emotions and atmosphere of the people and places around him, often reaping a healthy reward from the bereaved, who find solace in his comforting lies.

entries.name: Fey Prankster
entries.description: (Gathlain) Fey pranksters specialize in tricking others to teach a lesson or for their own entertainment.

entries.name: Filcher
entries.description: Whether cutting purses in the midst of combat or replacing prized items with fakes under the noses of their owners, the filcher is the master of the quick and quiet steal.

entries.name: Galtan Agitator
entries.description: Galtan agitators fight mightily to cast down the enemies of their ideals within the shambles of the tumultuous nation of a revolution-torn land.

entries.name: Guerrilla
entries.description: Guerrillas fight against oppressive leadership and governments including diabolic colonization in Sargava and the power structures in a diabolic empire proper, a shadow-bound land, and Razmiran

entries.name: Guild Agent
entries.description: Guild agents are members of a thieves’ guild or other shadowy organization. What they lose in independence, they more than make up for in benefits gained due to their association’s infrastructure.

entries.name: Gun Smuggler
entries.description: Gun smugglers are adept at procuring firearms and concealing their secret weapons

entries.name: Heister
entries.description: Notorious for their stealth, imagination, and elaborately planned thefts and capers, heisters specialize in breaking into secure locations, stealing items of value, and escaping undetected.

entries.name: Investigator
entries.description: Not all rogues work against the law. Investigators use their skills to serve the law, often in the employ of nobles or in the pursuit of noble causes.

entries.name: Kintargo Rebel
entries.description: Whenever the diabolic navy sails into the port, these rebels are quick to appear agreeably subservient in order to conceal their noncompliance and avoid retribution.

entries.name: Kitsune Trickster
entries.description: The kitsune trickster combines her sharpened wit with minor arcane powers of charm and persuasion.

entries.name: Knife Master
entries.description: The knife master is a trained killer who specializes in close-up combat and the wave and weave of knife fighting.

entries.name: Makeshift Scrapper
entries.description: Some combatants specialize in the study of certain weapons, but those without formal training often learn to survive a fight by making brilliant use of whatever is lying around.

entries.name: Master of Disguise
entries.description: A master of disguise believes that never letting her adversaries know her true identity protects her from bad luck or missteps on a job.

entries.name: Nameless Shadow
entries.description: Where bandits and tyrants prey on merchants and caravans, the nameless shadow preys on bandits and tyrants.

entries.name: Needler
entries.description: Needlers use subtlety and misdirection to deliver deadly poisons to unsuspecting victims in creative and unorthodox ways.

entries.name: Numerian Scavenger
entries.description: A Numerian scavenger lives for the discovery of new technological wonders scraped from the depths of the strange ruins, metal caverns, and outlandish junkyards of a realm of lost technology.

entries.name: Okeno Liberator
entries.description: The sight of yellow sails on the inner sea region signals the approach of a ship from Okeno, home port of the most ruthless and feared of all slaving operations. Most who see these sails flee in terror, but some freedom fighters actually endeavor to be captured, knowing that being taken to Stonespine Island in manacles is the easiest way to infiltrate the city, liberate other slaves, and lead them to freedom.

entries.name: Phantom Thief
entries.description: Phantom thieves come from the ranks of the elite, having grown bored with their finery, and seek thrills from acts of daring, skill, and crime.

entries.name: Pirate
entries.description: A pirate breaks from the confines of country and king to commit her crimes upon the high seas.

entries.name: Planar Sneak
entries.description: A planar sneak finds creative ways to defy conventional limitations when trying to overcome extraplanar obstacles.

entries.name: Poisoner
entries.description: The poisoner knows poison is just a tool toward an end, and is no different than any other weapon.

entries.name: Rake
entries.description: The rake is a rogue who is open about her skills and talents, often to the point of being boastful.

entries.name: Relic Raider
entries.description: Relic raiders are rogues who specialize in recovering treasures from ruins and tombs, some in a quest for knowledge, others out of a desire for riches.

entries.name: River Rat
entries.description: River rats are skilled at hiding amid reeds and roots, striking the unwary from the shallows as others would from the shadows.

entries.name: Roof Runner
entries.description: A specialized urban acrobat, the roof runner makes her home high atop the spires and gables of great cities.

entries.name: Rotdrinker
entries.description: Poisons are common tools in a rogue’s trade, and some poison-using rogues are so frequently exposed to these toxins that they have developed resistances to particular poisons.

entries.name: Sanctified Rogue
entries.description: The sanctified rogue serves a higher purpose, acting as a representative of a church or cult, or following the tenets of a specific faith or deity.

entries.name: Sapper
entries.description: The sapper is a trained siege engineer and can deal with traps and other obstacles given plenty of time.

entries.name: Scout
entries.description: Scouts frequently roam the wilderness, often banding together as bandits, but sometimes serving as guides, as trailblazers, or as companions to a ranger or barbarian warrior.

entries.name: Scroll Scoundrel
entries.description: Using knowledge from extensive research, the scroll scoundrel exploits overconfidence and predictability to better stay alive.

replaces: 2nd-level Rogue Talent, Trap Sense, Uncanny Dodge, Improved Uncanny Dodge, 10th-level Rogue Talent

entries.name: Sczarni Swindler
entries.description: If life is a game, the Sczarni play to win. When skill and luck aren’t enough, cheating is often the best option.

entries.name: Seeker of the Lost
entries.description: Aquatic elven adventurers descending into the ruins of sunken a lost empire developed techniques to ease their explorations, and they now share these techniques among a loose group of acquaintances calling themselves the seekers of the lost.

entries.name: Shadow Scion
entries.description: Shadow scions have learned the secrets of light and dark and draw power from the shadows themselves.

entries.name: Shadow Walker
entries.description: Shadow walkers are comfortable in light, darkness, and the shadows in between.

entries.name: Sharper
entries.description: Sharpers use trickery and deception to part an owner from his valuables.

entries.name: Skulking Slayer
entries.description: Pushed into a life of crime by the society around them, half-orcs gravitate toward criminal activities that suit them best.

entries.name: Sly Saboteur
entries.description: Sly saboteurs are irregular soldiers who specialize in sabotage and surprise attacks.

entries.name: Smuggler
entries.description: Smugglers specialize in moving contraband from one area to another while avoiding detection by authorities.

entries.name: Snare Setter
entries.description: Deep in darkness, the snare setter constructs his deadly traps and brutal mechanisms to confound and destroy any who try to invade his domain.

entries.name: Sniper
entries.description: Some say that the sniper is the worst kind of assassin: a killer who waits silently in the shadows and then strikes from a distance without remorse.

entries.name: Snoop
entries.description: Snoops act as information peddlers, specializing in gathering secrets through investigation, subterfuge, and coercion, and selling or trading those secrets for personal gain.

entries.name: Spy
entries.description: The best spies are like chameleons, but not only can they change their appearances to fit the situation, they can also change their personalities, allegiances, and even loves if that’s what it takes to achieve their clandestine goals.

entries.name: Survivalist
entries.description: The survivalist focuses her talents on surviving harsh and unforgiving conditions that would kill a lesser rogue.

entries.name: Swamp Poisoner
entries.description: (Grippli) Swamp poisoners use their own toxins to defend their homes and level the playing field

entries.name: Swashbuckler
entries.description: A paragon of mobile swordplay, the swashbuckler is a rogue who focuses almost exclusively on honing her skill at arms and perfecting daring acrobatic moves and elaborate flourishes that border on performance.

entries.name: Swordmaster
entries.description: A swordmaster meditates to strengthen her spiritual connection to her blade. She strives to perfect her skills by mastering six deadly trances.

entries.name: Sylvan Trickster
entries.description: Sylvan tricksters are rogues who model themselves after the mischievous fey of legend.

entries.name: Thug
entries.description: Some criminals steal with finesse, their victims only discovering the crime when the rogue is long gone and the coin already spent. A thug, on the other hand, cares nothing for finesse.

entries.name: Tidal Trickster
entries.description: Tidal tricksters roam the seas, using their skillful mastery of the currents to move across aquatic battlefields and throw their enemies off-balance.

entries.name: Toxic Talon
entries.description: A toxic talon spends resources and time combining easy-to-obtain materials into dangerous toxins to aid in the defense of a free nation.

entries.name: Trapsmith
entries.description: Some rogues are not content with just disabling traps—they love to build them, finding a captivating beauty in the turning of gears and the slither of ropes over pulleys.

entries.name: Underground Chemist
entries.description: Underground chemists are part of the rotting, fetid underbelly of the alchemical world.

entries.name: Vexing Dodger
entries.description: Vexing dodgers take advantage of their smaller size to outmaneuver larger foes such as giants.

entries.name: Waylayer
entries.description: A clever rogue knows the easiest battle to win is the one that’s over before your foe knows it has begun.

entries.name: Crossblooded
entries.description: A crossblooded bloodline combines the powers of two distinct heritages.

entries.name: Dragon Drinker
entries.description: (Requires Draconic Bloodline) The blood of dragons not only flows through a dragon drinker’s veins, but also empowers her spells and magical abilities when consumed.

entries.name: Eldritch Scrapper
entries.description: An eldritch scrapper is usually spoiling for a fight, looking to prove that she’s just as tough as a martial character.

entries.name: Mongrel Mage
entries.description: A mongrel mage is a sorcerer whose bloodline is so weak, or mixed with so many others, that her power isn’t clearly associated with any bloodline source.

entries.name: Nine-Tailed Heir
entries.description: eastern stories often tell of kitsune with multiple tails who have a magical quirk in their blood or have been blessed by their race’s deific matron, Daikitsu

entries.name: Razmiran Priest
entries.description: The Razmiran priest is a magical charlatan, missionary servant of the Living God.

entries.name: Seeker
entries.description: The seeker is obsessed with learning about their heritage and history, researching ancient texts and obscure ruins for clues.

replaces: Eschew Materials, 3rd-level Bloodline Power, 15th-level Bloodline Power

entries.name: Sorcerer of Sleep
entries.description: Some sorcerers have trouble accessing their innate gifts and must find another way to unlock them. For a sorcerer of sleep, the mind-altering drug pesh is the key.

entries.name: Stone Warder
entries.description: Stone warders have an innate ability to create runes that allow them to ward areas with magic traps built from their spells. These sorcerers are most common among dwarves, but have been known to appear among other races who have strong ties to earth, rock, stone, mountains, and the Darklands.

entries.name: Tattooed Sorcerer
entries.description: The tattooed sorcerer has embraced the ancient traditions of frontier spellcasting, and uses colorful and intricate tattoos to enhance her magical powers.

entries.name: Umbral Scion
entries.description: Umbral scions are sorcerers who are able to expertly control their especially potent shadow heritage. The majority of umbral sorcerers hail from the Darklands.

entries.name: Wildblooded
entries.description: A wildblooded sorcerer has a mutated version of a more common bloodline, with one arcana and at least one bloodline power that are different from those of an unmutated bloodline.

entries.name: Wishcrafter
entries.description: Wishcrafters are born with a talent for manipulating reality inherited from their efreeti ancestors.

entries.name: Arcane Bomber
entries.description: To many wizards, the experimentation of the alchemist seems quaint, if not dangerous or frightening. A few wizards take up the secrets of the bomb, however, fusing alchemy with their already considerable magical power.

entries.name: Arcane Physician
entries.description: Arcane physicians use their scholarly knowledge and arcane mastery to achieve incredible feats of medicine.

entries.name: Arcane Warden
entries.description: Arcane wardens are wizards who specialize in the discovery or generation of places of safety and refuge.

entries.name: Bonded Wizard
entries.description: Many wizards form an arcane bond with an item, but for some this bond becomes a powerful mystic union.

entries.name: Chronomancer
entries.description: Rare arcane scholars known as chronomancers demonstrate the ability to shift themselves in short bursts between the past, future, and alternate presents.

entries.name: Clocksmith
entries.description: Clocksmiths are oddities among wizard communities, pursuing the study and creation of clockwork constructs to near obsession

entries.name: Cruoromancer
entries.description: A cruoromancer infuses his necromantic magic with the power of his unique mixture of living blood and undead ichor.

entries.name: Elder Mythos Scholar
entries.description: Elder Mythos scholars risk their sanity to seek knowledge of alien and awful entities from beyond the stars.

entries.name: Exploiter Wizard
entries.description: Contrary to traditional wizardly study, an exploiter wizard forgoes the tried and true methods of arcane focus and arcane schools for the exploits favored by an arcanist.

entries.name: Familiar Adept
entries.description: Many wizards employ familiars to assist them, but only a few have unlocked the true power of their school of magic through the familiar itself.

entries.name: First World Caller
entries.description: Some wizards, typically First World gnomes, have mystical ties with the First World, the primordial home of the fey

entries.name: Hallowed Necromancer
entries.description: Many wizards study necromancy to create undead, but some study the same arts to purge the stain of undeath.

entries.name: Instructor
entries.description: Whether serving as staff at a formal school of magic or simply acting as a wandering teacher, an instructor has an apprentice who trades service to the instructor for lessons in magic.

entries.name: Pact Wizard (FF)
entries.description: Some wizards make bargains with beings from other realms in order to gain arcane power. These pact wizards have unparalleled access to extraplanar allies, but these bonds never come without strings attached.

entries.name: Pact Wizard (HHH)
entries.description: Wizards who seek mastery of arcane power without tedious study and monotonous research.

entries.name: Poleiheira Adherent
entries.description: Poleiheira adherents are wizards who wish to emulate the explorations and discoveries of Arustun and partake in great odysseys as they seek to imitate his achievements.

entries.name: Primalist
entries.description: A primalist is a wizard who has spent a considerable amount of time studying the chaos that is primal magic.

replaces: Arcane Bond, 5th-level Bonus Feat, 10th-level Bonus Feat

entries.name: Runesage
entries.description: Runesages draw upon the mystic energies of an ancient empire.

entries.name: Scroll Scholar
entries.description: Those who trade some of their potential to better understand ancient texts and scrolls can become learned scroll scholars.

replaces: Diviner's Fortune (diviner) or Hand of the Apprentice (universalist), 5th-level Bonus Feat, 4th-level spell slot

entries.name: Scrollmaster
entries.description: To some wizards, a scroll is not just a written form of a spell, it is a physical weapon meant to be used in combat like a sword or a shield.

entries.name: Shadowcaster
entries.description: Trained in the dark mysteries of a shadow-bound land's Umbral Court, the shadowcaster harnesses the power of shadows to bolster their spellcasting.

entries.name: Siege Mage
entries.description: The siege mage combines his arcane mastery with a supernatural link to siege engines.

entries.name: Spell Sage
entries.description: A spell sage has mastered spells of all types, and is able to increase the effectiveness of his own spells and eventually even cast spells from other classes’ spell lists.

entries.name: Spellbinder
entries.description: A spellbinder is an elven wizard who forges an arcane bond between himself and one or more wizard spells.

entries.name: Spellslinger
entries.description: While few contest the seductive allure of commanding arcane and occult powers, there are those wizards who become obsessed with the natural mysteries of black powder.

entries.name: Spirit Binder
entries.description: While most wizards learn their arts through gradual study, spirit binders have made a sudden arcane breakthrough due to the traumatic experience of losing a loved one.

entries.name: Spirit Whisperer
entries.description: Spirit whisperers are a breed apart among wizards, and are often mistaken for witches.

entries.name: Sword Binder
entries.description: Sword binders follow a tradition of martial wizards who often worked with the Church of a dead god and the crowns of a fading empire and then a diabolic empire.

entries.name: Undead Master
entries.description: Undead masters have great power over undeath.

entries.name: Wind Listener
entries.description: The wind listener takes a sylph’s natural curiosity to the extreme, enhancing his natural skill at subterfuge and eavesdropping with potent arcane magic.

entries.name: Worldseeker
entries.description: Worldseekers are wizards who travel to all corners of the Great Beyond.

entries.name: Armored Battlemage
entries.description: Armored battlemages learn to move and cast spells in even the most restrictive armors, and have developed new methods to magically enhance their armor.

entries.name: Beastblade
entries.description: Beastblade magi work in tandem with their familiars, using spell, steel, and claw to clear the battlefield of foes.

entries.name: Bladebound
entries.description: A select group of magi are called to carry a black blade—a sentient weapon of often unknown and possibly unknowable purpose.

entries.name: Card Caster
entries.description: The card caster is an ancient, martial offshoot of the traditional harrower, learning to not only draw power from the harrow, but also to invest each card with deadly power.

entries.name: Deep Marshal
entries.description: Largely unseen by visitors, the deep marshals have survived into the modern era as keepers, protectors, and repairers of the myriad of stony passages that travel around, through, and under the a dwarven mountain range.

entries.name: Eldritch Archer
entries.description: The eldritch archer rains magical attacks down on her foes from the city walls.

entries.name: Eldritch Scion
entries.description: Unlike typical magi, eldritch scions do not study tomes of magic or spend time learning to combine martial and magical skills. Rather, eldritch scions find that their spells and abilities come to them instinctively.

entries.name: Elemental Knight
entries.description: Elemental knights are born with elemental energies surging through their blood and discover the secret of reconciling and focusing this primal power into the arcane.

entries.name: Esoteric
entries.description: Esoterics are drawn to the mysticism of the occult and spend their lives delving into forgotten texts and forbidden tomes.

entries.name: Fiend Flayer
entries.description: Some tiefling magi can tap the dark energy of their fiendish blood to enhance their arcane and combat talents.

entries.name: Greensting Slayer
entries.description: The blending of martial prowess with elven magic has long been a staple of the Blackash Training Grounds in Erages. More than a few who study at Erages Academy follow this path because of the promises of wealth that the city’s criminal element makes toward practiced brawlers and smugglers.

entries.name: Hexbreaker
entries.description: Hexbreakers—sometimes called witch-hammers for their proclivity toward warhammers—have borne witness to the damage of unrestrained arcane power and hone their own arcane arts to battle such abuse.

entries.name: Hexcrafter
entries.description: A hexcrafter magus has uncovered the secret of using his arcane pool to recreate witch hexes.

entries.name: Iron-Ring Striker
entries.description: Practitioners of this martial art, powered by arcane magic, wear an iron ring on the finger of one hand.

entries.name: Jistkan Artificer
entries.description: As part of studying the secret methods the original Jistkan artificers used to build golems, these magi graft construct parts onto their own arms.

entries.name: Kapenia Dancer
entries.description: The kapenia dancer laces their deadly scarves with powerful magic.

entries.name: Kensai
entries.description: A kensai spends his life focusing his training and meditation into a rapturous perfection of the use of a single weapon, which is usually but not always a sword, channeling his arcane might through it in a dizzying and deadly dance beyond the abilities of even the greatest of mundane warriors.

entries.name: Magic Warrior
entries.description: Trained in a tradition stretching back to Old-Mage Jatembe’s Ten Magic Warriors, magic warriors renounce their identities to master magical might and serve as champions of culture and learning across the jungle-born Expanse and beyond.

entries.name: Mindblade
entries.description: A mindblade blends psychic talent and martial skill to lethal effect. By forming weapons with her mind, she always has the right tool for any situation.

entries.name: Myrmidarch
entries.description: The myrmidarch is a skilled specialist, using magic to supplement and augment his martial mastery.

entries.name: Nature-Bonded Magus
entries.description: A nature-bonded magus synergizes arcane magic and the divine magic traditions of druids into a deadly synthesis.

entries.name: Puppetmaster
entries.description: Puppetmasters focus on using charm and illusion spells to control the senses of those for whom they perform.

entries.name: Sigilus
entries.description: A sigilus manipulates the discoveries of wizards and other more sagacious Cyphermages, using those findings to create special sigils that allow her to transfer spell effects into different objects for later use.

entries.name: Skirnir
entries.description: Sometimes called a shield-vassal or shieldmaiden, the skirnir has learned to infuse his power into his shield.

entries.name: Sorrowblade
entries.description: A magus who has suffered greatly over the course ofher life can learn to channel that misery into her weapon and inflict it on others.

entries.name: Soul Forger
entries.description: The soul forger has learned the skill of infusing the raw magical essence of his soul into armaments of surpassing power, combining the mystic arts with the arts of war in a unity of steely perfection.

entries.name: Spell Dancer
entries.description: Many elven magi do not consider themselves masters of a blend of martial and magical talents, but rather a sub-category of wizards who study the effect of physical movement and techniques upon spellcasting ability.

entries.name: Spell Trapper
entries.description: Spell trappers forsake much of their arcane skill and martial knowledge in exchange for the ability to conjure magical traps to hinder their foes.

entries.name: Spellblade
entries.description: A spellblade magus can manifest a ghostly blade of force that can be used as an off-hand weapon.

entries.name: Spire Defender
entries.description: Magi who train themselves to accompany sages and archaeologists venturing into the Mordant Spire become spire defenders.

entries.name: Staff Magus
entries.description: While most magi use a one-handed weapon as their melee implement of choice, one group of magi uses the quarterstaff instead.

entries.name: Aerochemist
entries.description: Aerochemists use scraps of Shory’s magic in their concoctions to gain personal powers of flight.

entries.name: Alchemical Sapper
entries.description: Alchemical sappers are trained to create explosives.

entries.name: Alchemical Trapper
entries.description: Because kobolds rely on traps to soften up enemies, kobold alchemists learn to turn bombs into traps.

entries.name: Aquachymist
entries.description: Aquachymists are those rare few alchemists of land-dwelling and aquatic races alike who strive to unlock new and fantastic secrets of alchemy that can be discovered only in the water’s depths.

entries.name: Beastmorph
entries.description: Beastmorphs study the anatomy of monsters, learning how they achieve their strange powers.

entries.name: Blazing Torchbearer
entries.description: The blazing torchbearer is especially adept at manipulating flames of all kinds.

entries.name: Blightseeker
entries.description: Blightseekers are alchemists devoted to the study of fungi native to the Darklands.

entries.name: Blood Alchemist
entries.description: Most alchemists can transform matter and energy into other forms, but some wicked specialists realize that life itself is an energy that can greatly fuel their alchemy.

entries.name: Bogborn Alchemist
entries.description: Some grippli alchemists are particularly attuned to the swamps and the dangerous creatures that inhabit them; these serve as their laboratories and research subjects, respectively.

entries.name: Bramble Brewer
entries.description: Some half-elven alchemists merge human curiosity with their elven link to nature.

entries.name: Chirurgeon
entries.description: An alchemist who studies anatomy and uses this knowledge to heal is a chirurgeon.

entries.name: Clone Master
entries.description: Clone masters practice duplicating existing creatures in order to better understand how to create new life.

entries.name: Concocter
entries.description: Concocters are experts at combining sets of chemicals to create unique effects.

entries.name: Construct Rider
entries.description: A construct rider creates arcane devices to emulate and surpass weak flesh.

entries.name: Crimson Chymist
entries.description: Crimson chymists turn to the alchemical arts, infusing their bodies with the mutagenic essence of the Mantis God.

entries.name: Cruorchymist
entries.description: Cruorchymists see their blood as just another tool for their experiments

entries.name: Crypt Breaker
entries.description: Crypt breakers use their powers of perception and alchemical adaptation to safely investigate the mysteries of the past.

replaces: Alchemist Bomb, Mutagen, Brew Potion, Persistent Mutagen

entries.name: Deep Bomber
entries.description: Consumed with keeping hidden from the horrors below the surface, svirfneblin use their racial proclivity for alchemy and their inherent talent for obfuscation to strike their enemies from the darkness and retreat unseen.

entries.name: Dimensional Excavator
entries.description: Dimensional excavators have discovered and recorded ways to cause their bombs to create minor tears in the fabric of reality, forming extradimensional pits to vex their foes.

entries.name: Dragonblood Chymist
entries.description: The dragonblood chymist specializes in the reckless distillation of extracts and elixirs that allow them to experience the might of a dragon, however dangerous it might be .

entries.name: Ectochymist
entries.description: Ectochymists study the effects of alchemy on soul and spirit, focusing on fighting ghosts and other incorporeal creatures.

entries.name: Ectoplasm Master
entries.description: Alchemists capable of distilling spectral horrors into alchemical reagents.

entries.name: Eldritch Poisoner
entries.description: Eldritch poisoners are masters of the toxic arts, synthesizing lethal and incapacitating poisons with uncanny speed and expertise.

entries.name: Energist
entries.description: While most alchemists experiment mainly with chemicals and physical materials to create disparate effects, energists tap into the energy of life or death: positive energy or negative energy.

entries.name: Energy Scientist
entries.description: Energy scientists fervently prepare themselves to overcome exposure to specific elemental hazards so that they can traverse the Elemental Planes in search of novel discoveries and reagents.

entries.name: Fermenter
entries.description: Little more than moonshiners to some, fermenters focus their efforts on imbibing substances, learning from the resulting effects on their bodies, and infusing this knowledge into their skill sets.

entries.name: Fire Bomber
entries.description: Fire bombers are exceptionally good at using bombs to burn creatures and blow things up, but are not quite as good at creating other types of bombs or extracts.

entries.name: First World Innovator
entries.description: Those who can harness primal reagents—mundane reagents infused with the power of the First World—walk a fine line between genius and catastrophe.

entries.name: Gloom Chymist
entries.description: A breakthrough in Nidalese alchemy led to the creation of glooms, magical fields of darkness from the Shadow Plane that can be momentarily animated with the use of strange compounds.

entries.name: Grenadier
entries.description: Grenadiers sacrifice their skill with poisons in order to become more adept at using alchemical bombs.

replaces: Brew Potion, Poison Resistance, Poison Use, Swift Poisoning, Poison Immunity

entries.name: Grenadier [MC]
entries.description: Grenadiers train to exercise their talents in the thick of battle, even when not under the influence of their mutagens. They learn methods of combining weapon attacks with their alchemical magic, and sacrifice skill with poisons in order to become more adept at using alchemical bombs or using alchemical items in conjunction with their martial skills.

entries.name: Gun Chemist
entries.description: Simple alchemists may dabble in explosives, but for the rare gun chemist, a firearm’s barrel is his crucible

entries.name: Herbalist
entries.description: Vine leshys who study the physical and spiritual composition of their own bodies have discovered a strange herbal alchemy all their own.

entries.name: Homunculist
entries.description: One of the grand goals of alchemy is the ability to create new life. A homunculist has made this dream a reality, growing and modifying a familiar in his own laboratory.

entries.name: Horticulturist
entries.description: A horticulturist spends his time cultivating plants and plant creatures, allowing him to experiment with strange and wondrous herbal concoctions.

entries.name: Ice Chemist
entries.description: Reclusive alchemists who dwell in the highest mountains or on the frozen tundra devote their skills to mastering the cold.

entries.name: Inspired Chemist
entries.description: Akin to a mindchemistUM, inspired chemists use a type of cognatogen that instead of increasing their mental ability scores grants them inspiration like an investigator.

entries.name: Internal Alchemist
entries.description: An internal alchemist studies medicine, diet, and the living body to purify the self in the hope of gaining immortality.

entries.name: Interrogator
entries.description: An interrogator extracts vital information from reluctant individuals using alchemical and traditional methods.

entries.name: Mad Scientist
entries.description: The mad scientist’s colleagues laughed at her insights, mocked her theories, and hounded her from the halls of academia, simply because they were too weak and frightened to understand her work.

entries.name: Metamorph
entries.description: Metamorphs eschew traditional alchemy, focusing on internal chemistry and the transfiguration of living forms.

entries.name: Mindchemist
entries.description: A mindchemist can reach incredible levels of mental acuity, but suffers lingering debilitating effects to his physique.

entries.name: Mixologist
entries.description: Mixologists focus on mastering the chemical reactions between alcohol and the physical body.

entries.name: Mnemostiller
entries.description: Mnemostillers extract memories; hey can return memories as easily as administering a potion, and experienced mnemostillers create a variety of effects through the careful administration of past traumas or victories

entries.name: Oenopion Researcher
entries.description: The alchemist of Oenopion is incredibly skilled at making potions, elixirs, and other materials crucial to the country's economy and its monster-creating fleshforges.

entries.name: Oozemaster
entries.description: The oozemaster is a specialized alchemist who fights and ensnares oozes.

entries.name: Perfumer
entries.description: A perfumer alchemist refines extracts to their most pure and rarefied forms to spread on the wind

entries.name: Plague Bringer
entries.description: The plague bringer sees disease as the ultimate weapon, and has worked tirelessly to master new diseases and disease-delivery systems.

entries.name: Preservationist
entries.description: Some alchemists are obsessed with collecting and preserving exotic creatures.

entries.name: Promethean Alchemist
entries.description: Obsessed with discovering the origins of life, promethean alchemists build constructs they gradually endow with life.

entries.name: Psychonaut
entries.description: A psychonaut uses his knowledge to explore altered states of consciousness and even other planes of existence.

entries.name: Ragechemist
entries.description: Some alchemists create mutagens that tap into a primal anger that fuels their physical transformation.

entries.name: Reanimator
entries.description: A reanimator is an alchemist who has discovered how to infuse a corpse with a semblance of life.

entries.name: Royal Alchemist
entries.description: Many rulers often hire specialized alchemists capable of concocting protections from both poisons and diseases for the nobles and their guests.

entries.name: Saboteur
entries.description: The saboteur is an alchemist who specializes in destroying the plans, materials, and allies of his enemies.

entries.name: Sacrament Alchemist
entries.description: Sacrament alchemists serve in a great variety of priestly roles for their deities.

entries.name: Tinkerer
entries.description: Tinkerers constantly dabble in clockworking, creating special familiars that they regularly upgrade and with which they form bizarre bonds.

entries.name: Toxicant
entries.description: In lands such as a poisoners' city and a merchant nation where poisons are legal and may be openly studied and sold, some alchemists obsess over the myriad ways that poisons and venoms can be applied and delivered.

entries.name: Trap Breaker
entries.description: Trap breakers forgo the study of poison to instead master the construction and deployment of traps, using their nimble fingers to disable dangerous devices and their alchemical knowledge to create devastating land mines.

entries.name: Vaultbreaker
entries.description: The vaultbreaker combines stealth with his bomb-making talents to construct special focused charges that can disable or destroy hinges, locks, and similar mechanisms.

entries.name: Vivisectionist
entries.description: A vivisectionist studies bodies to better understand their function.

entries.name: Wasteland Blightbreaker
entries.description: The deleterious effects of the weird hazards of the a magic-blasted wasteland require special skill to remedy.

entries.name: Winged Marauder
entries.description: Goblin alchemists have created a mixture of pheromones that they use to manipulate and entice giant vultures or dire bats to do their bidding.

entries.name: Aeromancer
entries.description: While the practice of aeromancy is rare, some arcanists today are able to rival the aerial mastery of the ancient Shory aeromancers.

entries.name: Arcane Tinkerer
entries.description: Arcane tinkerers use their knowledge and understanding of magic to disrupt or even destroy constructs

entries.name: Blade Adept
entries.description: A small number of arcanists learn to use blades as part of their spellcasting and in combat.

entries.name: Blood Arcanist
entries.description: Though most arcanists possess only a rudimentary innate arcane gift, the blood arcanist has the full power of a bloodline to draw upon.

entries.name: Brown-Fur Transmuter
entries.description: Frequently called “brown-furs,” these transmutation-focused arcanists are known for transforming themselves into animals.

entries.name: Eldritch Font
entries.description: For some arcanists, the power bubbling up from within is nearly too much to contain.

entries.name: Elemental Master
entries.description: Arcanists with an affinity for elemental forces sometimes focus on one and display its power in everything they do.

entries.name: Harrowed Society Student
entries.description: Based out of a frontier land’s Twilight Academy, the secretive Harrowed Society focuses its efforts on the intellectual study of the region’s supernatural quirks and hidden history, and embraces the use of the harrow deck to examine the world’s occult mysteries.

entries.name: Magaambyan Initiate
entries.description: Aspiring students of the Magaambya often spend decades researching arcane magic while learning to follow in the footsteps of the academy’s founder, Old-Mage Jatembe.

entries.name: Occultist
entries.description: Not all arcanists peer inward to discern the deepest secrets of magic. Some look outward, connecting with extraplanar creatures and bartering for secrets, power, and favor.

entries.name: School Savant
entries.description: Some arcanists specialize in a school of magic and trade flexibility for focus.

entries.name: Spell Specialist
entries.description: Where most arcanists are broad in their study of magic, a spell specialist has her power focused in a few spells.

entries.name: Twilight Sage
entries.description: The twilight sages of an undead-ruled land carry out experiments to solve the ultimate puzzle and unlock the secrets of life and death. While the twilight sages generally aren’t actively malicious, most are willing to perform human experimentation in pursuit of knowledge with little regard for the casualties.

entries.name: Unlettered Arcanist
entries.description: Some arcanists store their spells as whispered secrets within familiars instead of on paper.

entries.name: White Mage
entries.description: A white mage is an arcanist touched by a divine power and gifted with the ability to heal others.

entries.name: Ancestral Harbinger
entries.description: While all bloodragers tap into their bloodlines to fuel the arcane energies they use in battle, some have the ability to call directly to the spirits of their ancestors to aid them, summoning spirits to fight for them or inspire their allies.

entries.name: Blood Conduit
entries.description: Blood conduits learn to channel their arcane might directly through their flesh, without the need for mystical words or gestures.

entries.name: Bloodrider
entries.description: In the world’s wild lands, a mount is an advantage in both everyday life and the dealing of death

entries.name: Bloody-Knuckled Rowdy
entries.description: The bloody-knuckled rowdy focuses on tricks and maneuvers that are quick and effective, duplicating combat styles from professional brawlers, street thugs, and even trapped animals.

entries.name: Crossblooded Rager
entries.description: While most bloodragers manifest only one bloodline, there are some that, through some quirk of heredity or the conjunction of other powers, manifest two.

entries.name: Enlightened Bloodrager
entries.description: Troubled by overwhelming rage and mystic forces beyond their comprehension, bloodragers have been traveling to the Magaambya for generations, seeking the peace and enlightenment promised by students of Old-Mage Jatembe.

entries.name: Greenrager
entries.description: Typically, nature finds its greatest harmony with divine magic, but sometimes a connection with the natural world manifest itself through the arcane current in the veins of the bloodragers called greenragers.

entries.name: Hag-Riven
entries.description: All changelings have the potential to transform into hags, but the process is a slow one, requiring several nights to complete. When left incomplete—by virtue of a wily changeling’s escape or her mother’s death—the creature is scarred and saturated in arcane power.

entries.name: Id Rager
entries.description: An id rager lacks a supernatural taint to his blood, instead drawing power from pure emotion.

entries.name: Metamagic Rager
entries.description: While metamagic is difficult for many bloodragers to utilize, a talented few are able to channel their bloodrage in ways that push their spells to impressive ends.

entries.name: Primalist
entries.description: While bloodrage powers come from the very essence of a bloodrager’s being and are often strict and immutable, some bloodragers tap into ancient traditions and primitive wisdom to enhance their rages with something more primal.

entries.name: Prowler at World's End
entries.description: Many catfolk bloodragers capable of communing with the ancient spirits of creation take on the burden of protecting the world from the sinister forces that exist at the world’s fringes.

entries.name: Rageshaper
entries.description: All bloodragers blend the unpredictable surge of arcane power with the savage fury of battle lust. For most, their rage is a conduit for the eldritch power locked in their heritage, but for a rageshaper, the latent magical energies in his blood bring about physical transformations and facilitate the blending of arcana and aggression into a deadly synthesis that few other barbarians (or even other bloodragers) can match.

entries.name: Spelleater
entries.description: Where other bloodragers learn to avoid or shrug off minor damage of all sorts, spelleaters tap into the power of their bloodline in order to heal damage as it comes, and can even cannibalize their own magical energy to heal more damage and continue taking the fight to the enemy.

entries.name: Steelblood
entries.description: Most bloodragers prefer light armor, but some learn the secret of using heavy armors.

entries.name: Symbol Striker
entries.description: Symbol strikers are unique form of rune-wielding berserker spellcasters whose tradition originates from Dongun Hold, a Sky Citadel in a gunpowder city

entries.name: Untouchable Rager
entries.description: While most bloodragers are known for their inexplicable ability to focus their bloodline into a horrifying mix of martial terror and spellcasting fury, from time to time a bloodrager’s bloodline acts differently.

entries.name: Urban Bloodrager
entries.description: Like the urban barbarian, the urban bloodrager has learned to control her rage in so-called polite society.

entries.name: Battle Dancer
entries.description: Battle dancers practice a martial art that emphasizes constant motion

entries.name: Bouncer
entries.description: Some taverns employ bouncers to keep out undesirables or for when their customers get too rowdy.

entries.name: Constructed Pugilist
entries.description: Brawlers that develop combat skills that use their prostheses so they always have a weapon at hand

entries.name: Exemplar
entries.description: A versatile soldier who inspires her companions with her fighting prowess, an exemplar is at home on the front lines of battles anywhere.

entries.name: Feral Striker
entries.description: A feral striker taps into a reservoir of druidic power hidden inside herself, allowing her to take animalistic characteristics.

entries.name: Hinyasi
entries.description: The hinyasi's martial traditions are centered on the use of farming tools and on other improvised weapons.

entries.name: Living Avalanche
entries.description: When a living avalanche is on the move, no one can stand in her way.

entries.name: Mutagenic Mauler
entries.description: Not content with perfecting her body with natural methods, a mutagenic mauler resorts to alchemy to unlock the primal beast within.

entries.name: Shield Champion
entries.description: Stalwart in battle, a shield champion has perfected an entire martial discipline relying on only her hand-to-hand fighting skills and her ever-present shield.

entries.name: Snakebite Striker
entries.description: With her lightning quickness and guile, a snakebite striker keeps her foes’ attention focused on her, because any one of her feints might be an actual attack.

entries.name: Steel-Breaker
entries.description: The steel-breaker studies destruction and practices it as an art form.

entries.name: Strangler
entries.description: A strangler is trained to choke the life out of her victims with her vise-like grip.

entries.name: Strong-Side Boxer
entries.description: A strong-side boxer employs a unique fighting style that incorporates a rope or cord wound around her hand.

entries.name: Turfer
entries.description: A turfer has a mastery over particular types of terrain.

entries.name: Ulfen Beast-Wrestler
entries.description: For these mighty grapplers, wrestling normal opponents has lost its challenge—they seek greater targets for glory.

entries.name: Venomfist
entries.description: Thanks to alchemical experiments and rigorous study of venomous creatures, a venomfist has toxic unarmed strikes.

entries.name: Verdant Grappler
entries.description: By accepting spirits of nature into her soul, a verdant grappler can entangle her foes with tangled undergrowth.

entries.name: Wild Child
entries.description: The wild child works with his sworn animal friend to conquer the challenges that lay before them.

entries.name: Winding Path Renegade
entries.description: Winding path renegades studied at the Houses of Perfection in an island nation, but while they grasped the mechanical aspects of the forms, they lacked the mental discipline required by the masters of the school.

entries.name: Beast Rider
entries.description: Where some cavaliers are simply skilled with horses or well-trained knights, the beast rider spends his life in constant pursuit of the most perfect mount, forming bonds with greater, more powerful, and more exotic creatures.

entries.name: Castellan
entries.description: A castellan is a cavalier who dedicates himself to the defense of a castle or walled city.

entries.name: Charger
entries.description: No warrior better epitomizes the centaur’s devastating martial power than the charger.

entries.name: Circuit Judge
entries.description: A circuit judge claims a specific region, becoming an expert in the local laws and, perhaps, becoming a fearsome executioner.

entries.name: Constable
entries.description: Constables keep order in the narrow streets and dark alleys of settlements.

entries.name: Courtly Knight
entries.description: These courtly knights are equally at home in a duel with words or swords.

entries.name: Daring Champion
entries.description: While many cavaliers are the champions of old fighting forms, some younger, more daring cavaliers mix a martial style influenced by the lighter armored and more flamboyant swashbuckler forms with the dedication of cavalier orders.

entries.name: Daring General
entries.description: Those cavaliers most gifted at command often become daring generals.

entries.name: Disciple of the Pike
entries.description: The a knight of a strict order Order of the Pike are renowned monster hunters, taking on large game using ancient weapon arts combined with modern equipment.

entries.name: Drakerider
entries.description: While many cavaliers dream of riding a dragon into battle, drakeriders come to learn that the reality involves far more effort than they had expected.

entries.name: Emissary
entries.description: Some cavaliers focus more on speed and mobility than they do on the raw power of the mounted charge.

entries.name: Esquire
entries.description: The esquire is a roving knight who acquires the services of a faithful follower—an aide-de-camp—who serves as the esquire’s assistant, spear carrier, and guard.

entries.name: Fell Rider
entries.description: The fell rider rides a bestial steed, a mount mastered by him alone. He tramples his enemies down, leaving twisted bodies in his wake, and fear rides with him.

entries.name: First Mother's Fang
entries.description: A first mother’s fang acts as a servant of his nation, a skilled general and tactician in times of war and a noble governor during times of peace.

entries.name: Gallant
entries.description: Gallants embody the virtues of honor, generosity, and civility. Their personal symbol serves as an inspiration to others in a courtly setting as much as on a battlefield.

entries.name: Gendarme
entries.description: The gendarme cares less for the finer points of tactical precision than he does for the exhilaration of the charge: the rush of wind through the visor of his helmet, the feel of his couched lance, the satisfying shriek of armor giving way before his weapon’s force as the point drives past metal into his foes.

entries.name: Ghost Rider
entries.description: Ghost riders are conflicted warriors who use the powers of the phantasmal dead even while seeking out and banishing the corruption of undeath from plagued communities.

entries.name: Green Knight
entries.description: Some knights serve nature itself and can be found protecting unspoiled natural places or serving fey beings.

entries.name: Herald Squire
entries.description: The herald squire is the eyes and ears of a traveling knight.

entries.name: Honor Guard
entries.description: Certain cavaliers are trained not as advance combatants, but as loyal guards, standing as firm defenders in the face of threats to their chosen charge.

entries.name: Hooded Knight
entries.description: Some cavaliers wander the lonely roads of the world—any world, including the First World—protecting travelers and acting as their honor guard.

entries.name: Huntmaster
entries.description: Huntmasters train the beasts favored by lordly castes into swift and deadly trackers.

entries.name: Hussar
entries.description: Agile and maneuverable cavalry, hussars make up for their relatively light armor with their speed and cunning.

entries.name: Knight of Arnisant
entries.description: The cavaliers known as knights of Arnisant revere the famous general who was crucial in the defeat of the Whispering Tyrant, the powerful wizard-king. Knights of Arnisant call upon Arnisant to grant them protection from evil magic, just as the Shield of a dead god protected him.

entries.name: Luring Cavalier
entries.description: Those who study the perfection of strategy and tactics know that picking the battlefield can grant advantages that only overwhelming numbers of allies can eclipse.

entries.name: Musketeer
entries.description: Some cavaliers are entrusted by their masters with the care and use of expensive and powerful oddities—firearms.

entries.name: Oceanrider
entries.description: Oceanriders are underwater cavaliers who ride dolphins, orcas, or seahorses.

entries.name: Qabarat Outrider
entries.description: The war colleges of the Castrovelian city-state of Qabarat produce a distinctive breed of cavalier known as the Qabarat outrider. In defense of the lashunta city-states, outriders lead small units of regular troops, the members of which can link minds with one another to form bonds in battle few can match.

entries.name: Saurian Champion
entries.description: These primeval cavaliers idolize dinosaurs as apex predators and value them as powerful, oversized mounts.

entries.name: Sister-in-Arms
entries.description: Some of the most charismatic Gray Maidens combine their devotion to their sisters with the intense tactical training they received, learning to perfectly direct their companions and inspiring them to survive and emerge victorious.

entries.name: Spellscar Drifter
entries.description: Spellscar drifters are self-reliant and always keep their firearms loaded—in the Spellscar Desert, a rider with a slow draw doesn’t live long.

entries.name: Standard Bearer
entries.description: Some cavaliers prefer to stand away from the fray, their banners a beacon shining brightly over the battlefield, rallying their troops to victory.

entries.name: Strategist
entries.description: Some cavaliers make a lifelong mission out of their exceptional ability to direct troops on the battlefield, combining tactical insight with a preternatural skill at improving the teamwork of their allies in order to win the day.

entries.name: Verdivant
entries.description: Some vine leshys’ spirits are vibrant enough to project this animus beyond their own bodies

entries.name: Vermin Tamer
entries.description: Due to the strange terrain, the lack of sunlight, and numerous other hazards, keeping a traditional mount in the Darklands can prove difficult. Cavaliers native to or traveling the region may choose to tame local creatures instead.

entries.name: Wave Rider
entries.description: Throughout the inner sea region, wave riders patrol harbors, keeping them safe from dangerous sea creatures and watching for smugglers. The most famous of these is the hippocampus-riding Sea Cavalry of a great city.

entries.name: Black Powder Vaulter
entries.description: Black powder vaulters like to get into the thick of the battle, maneuvering among the fray to find the most advantageous positions from which to kill their enemies.

entries.name: Blatherskite
entries.description: The blatherskate has an extraordinary talent for retreating from harm’s way and fooling his enemies into thinking he is weaker than he is.

entries.name: Bolt Ace
entries.description: While gunslingers are full of sound and fury, there is a class of gunslingers that never soil their hands with powder or feel the sting of gun smoke.

entries.name: Buccaneer
entries.description: Freebooters who cling to the convoluted codes that rule independent ships, the buccaneer is a gunslinger of the high seas.

entries.name: Bushwhacker
entries.description: The bushwhacker specializes in the art of the ambush. For her, gunplay works best when it comes from a concealed position and is directed against a target that falls with the very first volley and is dead before the smoke clears.

entries.name: Commando
entries.description: Commandos are those rough and ready gunslingers who excel at hit-and-run tactics and leveraging their expertise in the wild against their enemies.

entries.name: Experimental Gunsmith
entries.description: The experimental gunsmith is obsessed with creating the ultimate firearm, and is willing to take risks to work the kinks out of her design.

entries.name: Firebrand
entries.description: Where other gunslingers rely on precision shooting, the firebrand instead masters explosive ordnance.

entries.name: Graveslinger
entries.description: Graveslingers craft signature bullets to hunt down wandering undead. With this infused ammunition, they can take on the most resilient spectral foes with ease.

entries.name: Gulch Gunner
entries.description: These gulch gunners often specialize in proficiency with a single pistol (easily handled in tight spaces) and wander from warren to warren selling their tunnel-shooting skills to the highest bidder.

entries.name: Gun Scavenger
entries.description: A gun scavenger collects scraps, spare parts, and other components that might—if modified properly—give her firearm an extra edge.

entries.name: Gun Tank
entries.description: Gunslingers usually don’t use heavy armor, but there are a few who use and modify their armor to protect themselves from both traditional weapons and gunfire.

replaces: Bonus Feats (4th level and every 4 levels after)

entries.name: Gunner Squire
entries.description: The gunner squire is prepared to reload or repair her lord's firearms at a moment's notice.

entries.name: Maverick
entries.description: Quick with her gun and no stranger to barroom brawls, a maverick can hold her own when bullets and punches start flying.

entries.name: Musket Master
entries.description: Some gunslingers want a little more firepower and range. These are the musket masters; the best of these gunslingers can reload a musket with dazzling speed, potentially putting even their pistol-wielding brethren to shame.

entries.name: Mysterious Stranger
entries.description: A few rare gunslingers seem to accomplish their chosen tasks purely through willpower and an unwillingness to ever give up.

entries.name: Pistolero
entries.description: While most gunslingers have favorite firearms, there are those rare ones who choose to specialize in one-handed firearms exclusively.

entries.name: Planar Rifter
entries.description: Planar rifters harvest pieces of the Outer Planes, absorbing some of the energy into themselves and condensing other portions of it into bullets they can fire from their guns

entries.name: Scatter Gunner
entries.description: Punishing firearms such as the blunderbuss and dragon pistol can lay waste to invaders in tight corridors, and the dwarves of Dongun Hold have pioneered masterful methods for making the most of these indiscriminate weapons

entries.name: Siege Gunner
entries.description: The Grand Duchy of a gunpowder city has spawned all manner of firearm specialists, wielding small and large firearms alike. Siege gunners specialize in the very largest— cannons, bombards, and firedrakes.

entries.name: Techslinger
entries.description: Techslingers spurn unreliable gunpowder weapons in favor of high-tech armaments.

entries.name: Thronewarden
entries.description: As vigilant sentinels, thronewardens identify and head off trouble.

entries.name: Wyrm Sniper
entries.description: These long-shot artists are masters at taking down dragons with sharp shooting and light siege weaponry.

entries.name: Aquatic Beastmaster
entries.description: Hunters beneath the sea are just as committed as their surface-dwelling counterparts to working alongside their animal companions to eradicate threats.

entries.name: Chameleon Adept
entries.description: Some hunters are masters of blending into every situation, even making their companions appear humanoid for brief periods of time.

entries.name: Colluding Scoundrel
entries.description: The colluding scoundrel is a canny and conniving skirmisher, manipulating her enemies and leveraging her allies for her own benefit.

entries.name: Courtly Hunter
entries.description: While most hunters find themselves at ease in the wildest parts of the world, courtly hunters instead make their homes in cultured urban environments.

entries.name: Divine Hunter
entries.description: While most hunters heed the call of nature and fight to protect its bounty, some are inspired to serve a higher power.

entries.name: Feral Hunter
entries.description: A feral hunter has forged a bond with nature that’s so strong that she doesn’t merely channel the aspects of animals— she actually becomes an animal herself.

entries.name: Feykiller
entries.description: Some hunters in fey-plagued regions are dedicated to tracking down and eradicating these threats.

entries.name: Flood Flourisher
entries.description: Well adapted to their drenched surroundings, flood flourishers coordinate deadly ambushes with their loyal animal companions by capitalizing on their mastery of the soggy terrain.

entries.name: Forester
entries.description: While all hunters have a bond with the natural world, a forester has a stronger tie to her environment than to the animals within it.

entries.name: Packmaster
entries.description: Some hunters form bonds with packs of well-trained creatures. Whether such a hunter is a northern berserker running with a pack of timber wolves or a savage warrior dashing through the jungle alongside her herd of dimetrodons, the packmaster revels in the thrill of the hunt and the glory of the kill.

entries.name: Patient Ambusher
entries.description: Wandering the wilds, some hunters eschew the bond of innate teamwork with their animal companions. Instead, these hunters master the creation and deployment of intricate ranger traps, often using themselves or their animal companions to lure foes into their snares.

entries.name: Pelagic Hunter
entries.description: Pelagic hunters form strong bonds that extend deep beneath the sea.

entries.name: Plant Master
entries.description: Some hunters form a bond with plant life instead of an animal and take on those aspects instead.

entries.name: Primal Companion Hunter
entries.description: Most hunters are skilled at awakening the primal beasts inside themselves. However, some can instead activate the primal essence within their animal companion.

entries.name: Roof Runner
entries.description: Roof runners are skilled ambushers, skirmishers, and spies who eschew heavier types of armor in order to remain light on their feet.

entries.name: Scarab Stalker
entries.description: The forgotten ruins in the desert sands have given rise to a breed of hunters who call upon the powers of the pyramids to protect and explore the ancient sites of their people.

entries.name: Totem-Bonded
entries.description: Totem-bonded are hunters who are able to form a true spiritual bond with the powerful fauna that dominate the wildlands.

entries.name: Treestrider
entries.description: Some hunters are masters of the wild. Whether raised by apes or having some other link with simian creatures, these hunters glide through the wilderness with ease.

entries.name: Uprooter Scout
entries.description: The Uprooters are an elite band of an elven realm elves skilled and brave enough to foray into the Tanglebriar and take the offensive in the fight against Treerazer.

entries.name: Urban Hunter
entries.description: Urban hunters help guards track down and apprehend criminals or spies, find lost children and disaster victims, and protect animals from abuse in the city.

entries.name: Verminous Hunter
entries.description: A verminous hunter calls on the ceaseless, single-minded dedication of vermin to hunt and overwhelm her prey.

entries.name: Abolisher
entries.description: Abolishers are incorruptible inquisitors who weed out creatures of alien, unnatural origins, finding and exposing aberrations for what they are.

entries.name: Cloaked Wolf
entries.description: Some inquisitors are adept at appearing harmless until they throw off their unassuming facades and take their enemies by surprise.

entries.name: Cold Iron Warden
entries.description: The natural enemies of demoniacs and other cultists of fiendish forces, cold iron wardens are inquisitors who dedicate their lives to eradicating the taint of demonkind from the world.

entries.name: Exarch
entries.description: The gruff traditionalism of most dwarves finds its apex in those who adhere to a strict orthodoxy rooted in ancient principles and practices and who are not amenable whatsoever to change or innovation.

entries.name: Exorcist
entries.description: Some inquisitors, as they learn more about the threat of possession and the machinations of the planes, task themselves to expel possessing spirits and conniving outsiders from the world whenever possible.

entries.name: Expulsionist
entries.description: Expulsionists are inquisitors who seek to rid the material world of the corrupting influences of wicked spirits that twist mortals to their own ends.

entries.name: Faith Hunter
entries.description: Certain relentless inquisitors burn with special hatred for an enemy of specific convictions, and they stop at nothing when obsessively hunting these foes down.

entries.name: Green Faith Marshal
entries.description: The Green Faith marshal serves as a literal force of nature, hunting down and punishing those who have committed sins against nature through enslavement and mistreatment of animals or destruction of wild places.

entries.name: Heretic
entries.description: While all inquisitors hunt the enemies of the faith, sometimes, either through political maneuvering by her enemies or an unyielding tenacity that breaks her faith’s basic tenets, an inquisitor can find herself a heretic.

entries.name: Hexenhammer
entries.description: Hexenhammers learn to use the hexes and some spells of witches, but must pay the price for dealing with supernatural powers, as they slip ever closer to the evil they seek to destroy.

entries.name: Iconoclast
entries.description: Some magic items are heretical by nature, enabling the unfaithful to spread wickedness. Iconoclasts seek out and remove such crutches, cleansing the taint these items exude.

entries.name: Immolator
entries.description: The immolator puts her pyromaniacal urges to work in the service of a deity. She brings burning retribution down upon the enemies of her faith, consigning their souls to the sacrificial flames.

entries.name: Infiltrator
entries.description: This inquisitor uses guile and deception to blend in among the enemies of the faith rather than confronting them head-on.

entries.name: Keeper of Construct
entries.description: Some of Brigh’s inquisitors, and occasionally those who follow a god of the forge, track down malicious construct crafters and fight renegade constructs with unrivaled expertise.

entries.name: Keeper of the Current
